OVERTURE 1 from Northwest Georgia Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Revise BCO 14-2 to Permit Additional Ruling Elder Representation at the General Assembly"

Whereas, the PCA General Assembly ratio of Ruling Elders (RE) to  
Teaching Elders (TE) is in severe crisis, perhaps signaling a lack of  
support for GA among our Sessions [the numerical decline is apparent  
from the attached chart]; and  
Whereas, BCO 14-1 (9) calls for equal representation of TEs and REs on  
GA committees, exhibiting the value, principle, and prudence of parity,  
which assuredly applies to every level of the court; and  
Whereas, all other courts of the PCA have greater RE participation ratios  
than the steeply declining ratio at our General Assemblies (see also BCO  
8-9); and  
Whereas, the broader church may not support actions well (BCO 14-7) if  
adequate representation of the congregations and their Sessions are not  
present; and  
Whereas, the formula for GA representation (BCO 14-2) has not been  
updated since 1991 and may be altered by due process without  
disenfranchising others or affecting any other part of the constitution;  
and  
Whereas, the proposed formula herein could augment revenue for the GA,  
especially in conjunction with another overture to lower the registration  
fee for ruling elders (although we never wish to limit or depress ruling  
elders’ attendance due to revenue concerns); and  
Whereas, the proposed, if sent down to the presbyteries, would allow more  
ruling elders to voice their opinion on this potential increase in GA  
participation;

581

<a id="ga47-p584"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=584 printed_page=582 -->

Therefore, Northwest Georgia Presbytery overtures to amend BCO 14-2 to read (strike-through for deletions; underlining for new wording):

The General Assembly, which is a permanent court, shall  
meet at least annually upon its own adjournment. It shall  
consist of all teaching elders in good standing with their  
Presbyteries, and ruling elders as elected by their Session.  
Each congregation is entitled to four <del>two</del>—ruling elder  
representatives for the first 350 communing members or  
fraction thereof, and two ene-additional ruling elders for each  
additional 500 communing members or fraction thereof.

### So that it reads:

The General Assembly, which is a permanent court, shall  
meet at least annually upon its own adjournment. It shall  
consist of all teaching elders in good standing with their  
Presbyteries, and ruling elders as elected by their Session.  
Each congregation is entitled to four ruling elder  
representatives for the first 350 communing members or  
fraction thereof, and two additional ruling elders for each  
additional 500 communing members or fraction thereof.

Adopted by Northwest Georgia Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 3, 2018 Attested by TE P. Legree Finch, stated clerk

OVERTURE 2 from Northwest Georgia Presbytery (to CCB, CTS, OC) “Encourage CTS toward Growth and Release from Assembly Oversight”

Whereas, on several occasions, queries have arisen (either by overtures from the lower courts or from suggestions of various boards) if denominational educational institutions deserve different or more specialized oversight than the Permanent Committees of the PCA: and

Whereas, there may be valid institutional needs and opportunities among educational institutions that are limited by our current oversight, which is restricted to ordained officers; and

Whereas, other seminaries exist without oversight or support from a particular denomination and have the liberty to set their own standards for membership of their boards; and

Whereas, prospective ministerial students presently have many educational options, and removing formal oversight for one denominational seminary in no way threatens the quality of ministerial education— indeed, it could help other seminaries in their mission; and

Whereas, true liberty supports educational institutions in pursuing and adapting their mission, especially if they mature to a point where they do not wish to be exclusively under oversight by ordained officers; and

Whereas, we would not wish to restrict or hinder the true flourishing of fine faculties and institutions, nor encroach on academic freedom; and

<a id="ga47-p587"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=587 printed_page=585 -->

## APPENDIX V

Whereas, Covenant Theological Seminary (CTS) was founded in 1956, has been supported by PCA gifts since 1983, and is now both well established and capable of meeting its operating expenses; and Whereas, this libertarian option necessitates no changes in CTS personnel or operations, nor does it restrict any others from freely contributing to the mission and work of CTS:

Therefore, the 47th General Assembly approves a plan for releasing CTS from Presbyterian Church in America oversight and any accompanying restrictions, with a generous financial subsidy by encouraging all Sessions to give Askings for CTS for at least the next two years at the present rate. As such, when appropriate votes have been made, CTS will then be released from being an agency of the PCA (as per BCO 14-1) formally and as to any oversight, while all parties will continue to work together for mutually beneficial ends and in all ways possible; and Further, according to the process of BCO 26-2, to facilitate this, we recommend that the courts of the church vote to amend the BCO to read as below by simply deleting the reference to CTS in BCO 14-1.12 at the 47th General Assembly and during 2019-2020, followed by a similar vote on the RAO and By-Laws sections at the beginning of the 48th General Assembly once the BCO is amended to make those sections consistent [the relevant sections are RAO 4-3, 5-1(b)3, 5-2, 14-1, and Article VI-3 (which is simply to be deleted) of the Corporate By-Laws of Presbyterian Church in America (A Corporation)] with the amended BCO 14-1.12, while encouraging PCA churches to continue their giving to CTS in the future as they may. Accordingly, we overture to amend BCO 14-1.12 as follows, with the RAO and By Laws to conform afterwards:

12. The Assembly permanent committees are the Administrative Committee of General Assembly, Committee on Christian Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship. The Administrative Committee of General Assembly (AC) shall consist of <del>twenty (20</del>) nineteen (19) members:

- **a.** Eleven members in classes elected through the standard nomination and election procedure,

- **b.** One member each from the following program committees or agencies:

585

<a id="ga47-p588"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=588 printed_page=586 -->

1. Committee on Discipleship Ministries (CDM);

2. Covenant College (CC);

<del>3. Covenant Theological Seminary (CTS</del>);..

and renumber the other Committees or Agencies in this section, with the rest of this section remaining un-amended.

So that the 47th General Assembly amends BCO 14-1.12 to read:

12. The Assembly permanent committees are the Administrative Committee of General Assembly, Committee on Christian Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship. The Administrative Committee of General Assembly (AC) shall consist of nineteen (19) members:

- **a.** Eleven members in classes elected through the standard nomination and election procedure,

- **b.** One member each from the following program committees or agencies:

1. Committee on Discipleship Ministries (CDM);

2. Covenant College (CC)

3. Mission to North America (MNA);

4. Mission to the World (MTW);

5. PCA Foundation (PCAF);

6. PCA Retirement & Benefits, Inc. (RBI);

7. Reformed University Fellowship (RUF);

8. Ridge Haven Conference Center (RH). The eleven members at large shall serve a term of four years. The chairman of the Administrative Committee shall be one of its members at large. Each program committee and agency shall designate its member each year at the last meeting of the committee or board before the meeting of General Assembly. The chief administrative officers of the program committees and agencies may attend any meeting of the Administrative Committee. They shall be entitled to the privilege of the floor but shall not have a vote and must be excluded when an executive session is called.

586

<a id="ga47-p589"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=589 printed_page=587 -->

## APPENDIX V

Committee on Discipleship Ministries, Committee on Mission to North America, Committee on Mission to the World, and Committee on Reformed University Fellowship shall consist of fifteen (15) men divided into five classes of three men each, with two men being TEs and one RE or two men being REs and one TE on alternate years, elected to serve five-year terms. Committees on Discipleship Ministries, Mission to North America, Mission to the World, and Reformed University Fellowship shall have one ruling and one teaching elder as alternates to fill any vacancy that may occur during the year. Persons who have served for a full term, or for at least two years of a partial term, on one of the Assembly's permanent committees or agencies shall not be eligible for re-election to an Assembly committee until one year has elapsed. (Exceptions may be permitted in agency bylaws approved by the Assembly.)

Adopted by Northwest Georgia Presbytery at its stated meeting, August 18, 2018 Attested by TE P. Legree Finch, stated clerk

OVERTURE 3 from Northern New England Presbytery (to AC, CCB) "Amend RAO 10-3 to Promote the Exercise of Godly Prudence in Planning and Leading Times of Corporate Prayer and Worship at General Assembly"

Whereas BCO 47-5 states: "Public worship must be performed in spirit and in truth. Externalism and hypocrisy stand condemned. The forms of public worship have value only when they serve to express the inner reverence of the worshipper and his sincere devotion to the true and living God."; Whereas times of corporate worship and prayer at General Assembly should give expression to the unity of our church by providing an opportunity for all in attendance to call upon the Lord in sincerity and good conscience; Whereas the following sentences were used in a corporate confession of sin at the official pre-Assembly prayer gathering at the 46th General Assembly (2018):

587

<a id="ga47-p590"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=590 printed_page=588 -->

We grieve the disunity of your church. We grieve that many women in our congregations feel unvalued and unwanted, unheard and uncared for. We grieve that we have acted as though being male was more valuable than being female, that we have communicated that only men were wanted in service and care, that only male voices could be and should be heard, that only men were valued. We grieve not loving our mothers and sisters in Christ well. We grieve that the poor, the blue collar, the working class, and the middle class find our churches uninviting and unwelcoming. We grieve that we have played favorites, seeking to reach the wealthy and powerful with the Gospel while avoiding those who could not advance our influence. We grieve that our status symbols — cars, clothes, vacations, schools — have kept people away from the very place where we declare that he who was rich became poor for our sakes so that we might be rich in him. We grieve that black and brown people have found our churches to be overwhelming and unsympathetic places, more loyal to “whiteness" than to the red blood of Jesus shed on the Cross. We grieve that our loyalties to politicians who play on racial fears have been stronger than our loyalties to our black and brown brothers and sisters in Christ. We grieve that we have wittingly and unwittingly erected once again the very wall of hostility that Christ's cross had torn down. We grieve that those who have spoken the Gospel truth on our racial unity-indiversity have been shouted down as “cultural Marxists” or “social justice warriors” rather than celebrated as servants of the Gospel. Whereas many PCA officers and members do not think that they are guilty of the specific sins mentioned in the above sentences, nor do they agree with some of the assumptions that seem to be implied in these sentences, and therefore they would not be able to pray these things in sincerity and good conscience; Whereas other controversial practices and ideas have been included in times of corporate worship and prayer at previous General Assemblies; Therefore be it resolved, that the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America amend RAO 10-3 by adding the following sentence (additions are underlined):

588

<a id="ga47-p591"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=591 printed_page=589 -->

## APPENDIX V

10-3. Worship services shall be included as approved by the Assembly. The Administrative Committee must approve any non-PCA speaker. Those involved in the organization and leadership of times of corporate worship and prayer at General Assembly are to exercise godly prudence as they strive to ensure that all that is said and done at these gatherings gives expression to the unity of our church by providing an opportunity for all in attendance to call upon the Lord in sincerity and good conscience. The newly amended section would then read as follows: 10-3. Worship services shall be included as approved by the Assembly. The Administrative Committee must approve any non-PCA speaker. Those involved in the organization and leadership of times of corporate worship and prayer at General Assembly are to exercise godly prudence as they strive to ensure that all that is said and done at these gatherings gives expression to the unity of our church by providing an opportunity for all in attendance to call upon the Lord in sincerity and good conscience.

OVERTURE 4 from Calvary Presbytery (to OC) “Declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's ‘Nashville Statement' on Biblical Sexuality as a Biblically Faithful Declaration"

Whereas the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's "Nashville Statement" declares: Article 1 WE AFFIRM that God has designed marriage to be a covenantal, sexual, procreative, lifelong union of one man and one woman, as husband and wife, and is meant to signify the covenant love between Christ and his bride the church. WE DENY that God has designed marriage to be a homosexual, polygamous, or polyamorous relationship. We also deny that marriage is a mere human contract rather than a covenant made before God.

589

<a id="ga47-p592"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=592 printed_page=590 -->

Article 2 WE AFFIRM that God's revealed will for all people is chastity outside of marriage and fidelity within marriage. WE DENY that any affections, desires, or commitments ever justify sexual intercourse before or outside marriage; nor do they justify any form of sexual immorality. Article 3 WE AFFIRM that God created Adam and Eve, the first human beings, in his own image, equal before God as persons, and distinct as male and female. WE DENY that the divinely ordained differences between male and female render them unequal in dignity or worth. Article 4 WE AFFIRM that divinely ordained differences between male and female reflect God's original creation design and are meant for human good and human flourishing. WE DENY that such differences are a result of the Fall or are a tragedy to be overcome. Article 5 WE AFFIRM that the differences between male and female reproductive structures are integral to God's design for selfconception as male or female. WE DENY that physical anomalies or psychological conditions nullify the God-appointed link between biological sex and self-conception as male or female. Article 6 WE AFFIRM that those born with a physical disorder of sex development are created in the image of God and have dignity and worth equal to all other image-bearers. They are acknowledged by our Lord Jesus in his words about “eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb." With all others they are welcome as faithful followers of Jesus Christ and should embrace their biological sex insofar as it may be known. WE DENY that ambiguities related to a person's biological sex render one incapable of living a fruitful life in joyful obedience to Christ. Article 7 WE AFFIRM that self-conception as male or female should be defined by God's holy purposes in creation and redemption as revealed in Scripture. 590

<a id="ga47-p593"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=593 printed_page=591 -->

## APPENDIX V

WE DENY that adopting a homosexual or transgender selfconception is consistent with God's holy purposes in creation and redemption. Article 8 WE AFFIRM that people who experience sexual attraction for the same sex may live a rich and fruitful life pleasing to God through faith in Jesus Christ, as they, like all Christians, walk in purity of life. WE DENY that sexual attraction for the same sex is part of the natural goodness of God's original creation, or that it puts a person outside the hope of the gospel. Article 9 WE AFFIRM that sin distorts sexual desires by directing them away from the marriage covenant and toward sexual immorality— a distortion that includes both heterosexual and homosexual immorality. WE DENY that an enduring pattern of desire for sexual immorality justifies sexually immoral behavior. Article 10 WE AFFIRM that it is sinful to approve of homosexual immorality or transgenderism and that such approval constitutes an essential departure from Christian faithfulness and witness. WE DENY that the approval of homosexual immorality or transgenderism is a matter of moral indifference about which otherwise faithful Christians should agree to disagree. Article 11 WE AFFIRM our duty to speak the truth in love at all times, including when we speak to or about one another as male or female. WE DENY any obligation to speak in such ways that dishonor God's design of his image bearers as male and female. Article 12 WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ gives both merciful pardon and transforming power, and that this pardon and power enable a follower of Jesus to put to death sinful desires and to walk in a manner worthy of the Lord. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ is insufficient to forgive all sexual sins and to give power for holiness to every believer who feels drawn into sexual sin.

591

<a id="ga47-p594"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=594 printed_page=592 -->

Article 13 WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ enables sinners to forsake transgender self- conceptions and by divine forbearance to accept the God-ordained link between one's biological sex and one's self-conception as male or female. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ sanctions selfconceptions that are at odds with God's revealed will. Article 14 WE AFFIRM that Christ Jesus has come into the world to save sinners and that through Christ's death and resurrection forgiveness of sins and eternal life are available to every person who repents of sin and trusts in Christ alone as Savior, Lord, and supreme treasure. WE DENY that the Lord's arm is too short to save or that any sinner is beyond his reach. Therefore be it resolved that the Calvary Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly and asks it to declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's "Nashville Statement" on biblical sexuality as a biblically faithful declaration and refer the “Nashville Statement” to the Committee on Discipleship Ministries for inclusion and promotion among its denominational teaching materials. Grounds: “The Nashville Statement," carefully worked out by the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood in 2017, is a timely statement that speaks into the current confusion surrounding gender and sexuality within the evangelical church (including the PCA) and the broader culture. Signed by many leaders within the Reformed and evangelical world, it is a balanced and biblically faithful attempt to “speak the truth in love" (Eph. 4:15) on one of the most pivotal and controversial issues facing the church today. Additionally, “The Nashville Statement” clearly reiterates the truth of foundational passages of Scripture and our confessional understanding of marriage, gender, and sexual ethics. It affirms God's good purpose in ordaining the binary nature of gender while bestowing His image on mankind (Gen. 1:27), His design for marriage between one biological man and one biological woman (Gen. 1:23, 24), and the sinfulness of homosexual and transgender desire as well as conduct (Mat. 15:18, 19; I Cor. 6:9-11). In addition to affirming these historic, orthodox truths, the Nashville Statement also lifts up the hope of the gospel to the sexual struggler, pointing the reader to our Lord Jesus Christ as “the double cure," saving us both from sin's guilt

592

<a id="ga47-p595"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=595 printed_page=593 -->

## APPENDIX V

and power. Therefore, the PCA would do well to commend “The Nashville Statement" and prepare it for distribution through Committee on Discipleship Ministries. Adopted by Calvary Presbytery at its stated meeting, October 25, 2018 Attested by /s/ RE Melton L. Duncan, stated clerk

OVERTURE 5 from Central Indiana Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 23-1 on Procedures for Dissolving Various Pastoral Relations"

Central Indiana Presbytery hereby overtures General Assembly to amend BCO 23-1 as follows in order to clarify the procedures for the dissolution of the various pastoral relations: 23-1. When any minister shall tender the resignation of his pastoral charge to his Presbytery, the Presbytery shall cite the church to appear by its commissioners, to show cause why the Presbytery should or should not accept the resignation. If the church fails to appear, or if its reasons for retaining its pastor be deemed insufficient, his resignation shall be accepted and the pastoral relation dissolved. If any church desires to be relieved of its pastor, <del>a similar</del> <del>procedure shall be observed. But whether the minister or the</del> <del>church initiates proceedings for a dissolution of the relation</del>, <del>there shall always be a meeting of the congregation called and</del> <del>conducted in the same manner as the call of the pastor. In any</del> <del>case</del>, or associate pastor, a congregational meeting must first be called for the purpose of voting on the proposed dissolution. If the proposed dissolution is approved, the church shall present its request to the Presbytery, and the Presbytery shall make a final determination regarding the proposed dissolution. In the case of an assistant pastor, the church Session may present its request for dissolution directly to the Presbytery without prior approval at a congregational meeting. In all cases, the minister must not physically leave the field until the Presbytery or its commission empowered to handle uneontested-requests for dissolution has dissolved the relation. The associate or assistant pastors may continue to serve a congregation when the pastoral relation of the senior pastor is dissolved, but they may not normally succeed the senior pastor 593

<a id="ga47-p596"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=596 printed_page=594 -->

without an intervening term of service in a different field of labor. However a congregation by a secret ballot with fourfifths (4/5) majority vote may petition Presbytery for an exception which by a three-fourths (3/4) majority vote Presbytery may grant. Presbytery needs to determine if the dissolution of the pastoral relationship with the senior pastor was brought about in Christian love and good order on the part of the parties concerned. Rationale: The current language in the second paragraph of BCO 23-1 is unclear regarding the proper procedure for a congregation to pursue in the interest of dissolving the different pastoral relations. As it currently stands, it could be understood to imply that even in the case of an assistant pastor, who is called only by the Session and not the congregation (BCO 22-3), the congregation must first vote to approve the dissolution before the request to dissolve the relationship is presented to the Presbytery. The proposed amendment simply seeks to clarify the proper procedure in the case of a pastor, associate pastor, or assistant pastor.

Adopted by Central Indiana Presbytery at its stated meeting, September 14, 2018 Attested by TE Kristofer D. Holroyd, stated clerk

But in such instances, the OC would act in many regards like a committee of commissioners.

RAO 12-1. The permanent Committees and Agencies, special committees, and ad interim committees of the Assembly shall make annual reports, which shall be transmitted to the Stated Clerk by at least ninety (90) days prior to the opening of the General Assembly. The Stated Clerk shall refer these reports to the relevant committee of commissioners for their review and recommendation to the General Assembly (cf. 14-6; 14-7). and ad interim committees shall report directly to the General Assembly without reference to a committee of commissioners. However, all recommendations proposing amendment to the Constitution shall be referred to the Overtures Committee for their review and recommendation to the General Assembly under the rules governing a committee of commissioners as applicable (RAO 14-6.d-k; 14-7.c-d; 14-9.d-h). [Emphasis added. See also RAO 15-1.4] The OC would function under certain RAO 14 rules, instead of entirely under RAO 15 rules (i.e., the fifteen paragraphs from RAO 14 cited in the parenthesis). Thus, if any of those fifteen provisions stipulate something different than what is stipulated in RAO Chapter 15 (Overtures Committee), the RAO 14 (Committee of Commissioners) provision governs. One difference, for example, regards the allowance or disallowance of an OC minority report. RAO 15-6.s allows minority reports from the OC when the OC is acting in its ordinary RAO 15 capacity. But RAO 14-6.h prohibits minority reports from committees of commissioners. And since RAO 14-6.h is included in the parenthetical list in RAO 12-1, that prohibition would govern the OC when it reports a recommendation on a constitutional amendment proposed by any study committee. Presumably, this is because a substitute motion from a Committee of Commissioners is like a minority report when it proposes something different from what is proposed by a Permanent Committee. Likewise, a substitute recommendation from the OC would be akin to a minority report on a GAappointed Study Committee recommendation. In the event there was a minority report from a study committee on a proposed constitutional amendment, the OC would also consider it. The OC would report recommendations on each to the GA.

And if the OC recommends a substitute for a constitutional amendment proposed by the study committee, the procedures and time limits for debate are the same as those for handling an OC minority report on an ordinary OC recommendation (i.e., RAO 14.9.h.1-3 and RAO 15-8.g.1-3).

OVERTURE 8 from Ohio Valley Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 14-1.10, 14-1.11, and 14-1.12 to Allow Non-ordained Persons to serve on Committees and Boards"

Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America believes Christ has called his church to be a “spiritual commonwealth” (BCO 3-1), in which members elect godly men to be ordained as elders who are given the power of jurisdiction as they act jointly in the courts of the church (BCO 3-2); and Whereas, a robustly complementarian perspective affirms the oversight of these elders and the proper, vital, and full expression of the gifts given by Christ to men and women for his service; and Whereas, vigorous participation of women in the life of the early church is attested by the New Testament: they helped select (Acts 1:14) and train (Acts 18:26) leaders of the church, prophesied (Acts 21:8-9), served the church through deeds of mercy in vital ways (Acts 9:36–41), were instrumental in the planting of churches (Acts 16:12–15; 17:4,12) and

601

important leaders for the church (Rom. 16:3-4); and  
Whereas, as part of the calling of church leaders to “equip the saints for the  
work of ministry for building up the body of Christ" (Eph. 4:12), sessions  
throughout the PCA identify gifted men and women to serve on  
committees of the church, such as missions, building, and pastoral search  
committees; and  
Whereas, in contrast with a commission in the PCA, which is "authorized to  
deliberate and conclude the business referred to it," committees are  
appointed by courts "to examine, consider and report" to their  
constituting court concerning the matters that court delegates to them  
(BCO 15-1) and thus do not exercise governing authority; and  
Whereas, in accordance with this principle, Permanent Committees  
established by the General Assembly are “to serve and not to direct any  
Church judicatories. They are not to establish policy, but rather execute  
policy established by the General Assembly" (BCO 14-1.7); and  
Whereas, these considerations suggest there is no impediment to an  
unordained member in good standing in the PCA serving on a Permanent  
Committee of the General Assembly established in BCO 14-1.12; and  
Whereas, the 45th General Assembly adopted the recommendation of The  
Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church  
that stated, "sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly strive to  
develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom  
of godly women in the local, regional, and national church, and  
particularly consider overtures that would allow qualified women to  
serve on appropriate committees and agencies within the church";  
Therefore be it resolved to amend The Book of Church Order by deleting  
14-1.10; by amending 14-1.11 as follows (and renumbering as 14-1.10);

OVERTURE 9 from Platte Valley Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 42-4; 43-2; 43-3 regarding Method and Deadlines of Filing Cases"

Whereas, the Standing Judicial Commission ruled in Case 2016-02  
(M45GA, 2017, pp. 510–14), that notice of complaints must be made by  
hard copy, and that electronic filing of complaints are administratively  
out of order; and  
Whereas, the language of both BCO 42-4 (filing appeals) and BCO 43-3  
(filing complaints) confusingly refer to two kinds of notification: the  
notification of the lower court's original decision, and the notification of  
appeal/complaint by the appellant/ complainant; and  
Whereas, BCO 42-4 and BCO 43-3 explicitly provide that the “notification”  
(that is, the notification of the lower court's original decision) may be  
made electronically, but do not explicitly forbid notification of appeals  
and complaints from being made electronically; and  
Whereas, BCO 43-2 does not describe multiple types of “notification," but  
still does not explicitly define that complainants may not file a complaint  
electronically; and  
Whereas, the Operating Manual (18.10.b) of the Standing Judicial  
Commission much more clearly defines proper, timely filing:  
Documents required or permitted to be filed by a party shall be  
filed with the Stated Clerk. Such filing shall not be timely  
unless the documents are received in the office of the Stated  
Clerk within the time fixed for such filing, except that papers  
shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing if certified,  
registered or express mail of the United States Postal Service  
or any private service where verifying receipt is utilized.  
Neither facsimiles nor Email will be allowed for purposes of  
filing. Interested parties should be aware that responsibility for  
such filings rests with them and that delays in delivery or non-  
delivery are the sole responsibility of the filing party.  
and  
Whereas, this language would also help Sessions and Presbyteries clarify  
proper, timely filing of appeals and complaints if included in the BCO;  
and  
Whereas, the authors of the SJC Concurring Opinion on Case 2016-02  
acknowledged this confusion of language, writing, "Accordingly we  
believe that BCO 43-3 should be clarified by amendment offered through  
an Overture” (M45GA, 2017, p. 514);

608

<a id="ga47-p611"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=611 printed_page=609 -->

Therefore, Platte Valley Presbytery overtures to amend BCO 42-4 to read (<del>strikethrough</del> for deletions; underlining for new words):

42-4. Notice of appeal may be given the court before its  
adjournment. Written notice of appeal, with supporting  
reasons, shall be filed by the appellant with both the clerk of  
the lower court and the clerk of the higher court, <del>within thirty</del>  
(<del>30) days of notification of the last court's decision</del>. Such filing  
shall not be timely unless the documents are received by the  
clerk of the lower court and the clerk of the higher court within  
thirty (30) days of notification of the last court's decision,  
except that papers shall be deemed filed on the day of mailing  
if certified, registered or express mail of the United States  
Postal Service or any private service where verifying receipt is  
utilized. Neither facsimiles nor e-mail will be allowed for  
purposes of filing. Interested parties should be aware that  
responsibility for such filings rests with them and that delays  
in delivery or non-delivery are the sole responsibility of the  
filing party.

Notification of the last court's decision shall be deemed to have  
occurred on the day of mailing (if certified, registered or  
express mail of a national postal service or any private service  
where verifying receipt is utilized), the day of hand delivery,  
or the day of confirmed receipt in the case of e-mail or  
facsimile. Furthermore, compliance with such requirements  
shall be deemed to have been fulfilled if a party cannot be  
located after diligent inquiry or if a party refuses to accept  
delivery. No attempt should be made to circularize the courts  
to which appeal is being made by either party before the case  
is heard.

## APPENDIX V

OVERTURE 10 from Northern New England Presbytery (to OC, AC) "Appoint Ad Interim Committee on Domestic Abuse and Sexual Assault"(Version 2)

Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25- 27; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are "against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society;5 and Whereas, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and

5For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: "More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime" (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/ accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online at http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf) 613

<a id="ga47-p616"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=616 printed_page=614 -->

Whereas, the Rules of Discipline protect against unjust accusation (BCO 31- 8), they also make no consideration for the unique heinousness of the sins and their practical effect on the victims; Therefore be it resolved that Northern New England Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the nature and causes of domestic abuse and sexual assault;

- **(2)** the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins as well as ministry and counsel for those overtaken by these sins;

- **(3)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(4)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with Northern New England Presbytery committed to offer $1,000, and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly. Adopted by Northern New England Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 2, 2019 Attested by TE C.S. Per Almquist, stated clerk

OVERTURE 11 from Fellowship Presbytery (OC, AC, CDM, CC, RUF) “Commend and Distribute RPCNA's Contemporary Perspectives on Sexual Orientation: A Theological and Pastoral Analysis" Whereas it is the responsibility of the General Assembly to evaluate needs for the most effective fulfillment of the Great Commission (BCO 14- 1.5); and Whereas the General Assembly has been given the power in general to recommend measures for the promotion of charity, truth, and holiness through all the churches under its care (BCO 14-6.k); and Whereas the local Sessions are tasked with shepherding the flock in their midst (1 Peter 5:2), and saving others by snatching them out of the fire, showing mercy to others with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh (Jude 23); and

614

<a id="ga47-p617"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=617 printed_page=615 -->

## APPENDIX V

Whereas much of the flock in our midst has often been exposed to great  
depths of evil through the ubiquitous presence of the internet, the  
sexualization of entertainment, broadening sexual ethics in the court  
system, and increasing globalization; and  
Whereas some of the flock in our midst are hard-pressed with temptation  
that manifests itself through same sex attraction or a confused sexual  
identity (Rom 1:26); and  
Whereas some elders, deacons, or sessions may feel overwhelmed or  
underequipped to minister to those in their flock that struggle with these  
unholy desires; and  
Whereas the topic of sexual orientation needs clarification, and is as yet an  
uncovered topic in PCA reports; and  
Whereas a NAPARC member church, the Reformed Presbyterian Church  
North America (RPCNA), has produced an excellent resource on this  
issue that is both exegetically sound and pastorally tender entitled  
“Contemporary Perspectives on Sexual Orientation: A Theological and  
Pastoral Analysis"; and  
Whereas at the 44th General Assembly the Cooperative Ministries  
Committee, though unable to make direct recommendations to the  
Assembly, commended this RPCNA report to be read and studied by  
teaching elders and Sessions (M44GA, p. 334);  
Therefore, be it resolved that the General Assembly receive “Contemporary  
Perspectives on Sexual Orientation: A Theological and Pastoral  
Analysis" (available on pages 86-131 at http://rparchives.org/  
data/Minutes%20of%20 Synod/2011%20 Minutes.pdf) and distribute it  
to the presbyteries and congregations of the denomination; and  
Be it further resolved that the General Assembly direct the Committee on  
Discipleship Ministries to publish the CPSO for sale and distribution,  
along with the other actions of the Assembly related to human sexuality,  
especially the actions of the 5th General Assembly and the Joining and  
Receiving, as the PCA's statements on the Gospel and human sexuality;  
and  
Be it further resolved that the General Assembly direct the Committee on  
Discipleship Ministries to assist sessions in the watching over their flock  
and in the nourishing and guarding of the children of the church by  
creating a resource or curriculum based on the CPSO report that could  
be used with students that might be struggling with issues related to  
sexual identity, same sex attraction, or gender confusion; and  
Be it further resolved that the General Assembly direct Reformed  
University Fellowship to participate in promoting the prosperity and  
enlargement of the Church by incorporating CPSO in their annual  
training; and

615

<a id="ga47-p618"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=618 printed_page=616 -->

Be it further resolved that the General Assembly direct Covenant College to nourish and safeguard the young people of the church by making this report available to faculty, staff, and students, as well as including the content of this report in the life of the school in some fashion (perhaps through RA training, chapel, or other venues); and Be it further resolved that the General Assembly encourage Sessions and elders to be active in shepherding those in their flock that struggle against same sex attraction or sexual confusion so that elders might keep watch over their flocks as ones who will give an account, and that we all might win a full reward (Heb. 13:17; 2 John 8). Adopted by Fellowship Presbytery at its stated meeting, January 26, 2019 Attested by TE Robert F. Sprinkle Jr., stated clerk

OVERTURE 12 from Northern New England Presbytery  
y (to CCB, OC)  
“Amend RAO 8-4 regarding Floor Nominations”  
Whereas, subjection to the brethren is an oath taken by both Teaching and  
Ruling Elders in the PCA (BCO 21-5.6; 24-6.5) and such subjection  
begins with those brothers closest in relationship to said officer; and  
Whereas, our form of government seeks to give deference to and maintain  
the authority of lower courts; and  
Whereas, floor nomination of officers to fill open positions on the Permanent  
Committees, Agencies, and the Standing Judicial Commission of the  
General Assembly are, by definition, not made through such lower  
courts; and  
Whereas, the rise of celebrity officers within Christ's Church is a worrisome  
trend that can lead to polarization and division within Christ's body  
(1 Corinthians 1:10-14); and floor nominations can serve as an avenue  
for the furtherance of this trend; and  
Whereas, the undertaking of service within the Agencies and Committees of  
the General Assembly is one to be considered with deliberation and  
prayer; and  
Whereas, the Nominating Committee is entrusted with the important task of  
evaluating and nominating  
Therefore be it resolved, Northern New England Presbytery hereby  
overtures the 47th General Assembly to restrict floor nominations at the  
General Assembly for the Assembly Committees and Agencies to those  
whose names were submitted to the Nominating Committee according  
to RAO 8-4.d and e, by adding a final sentence to RAO 8-4.i as indicated  
below. [Addition indicated by underlining.]

616

<a id="ga47-p619"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=619 printed_page=617 -->

## APPENDIX V

RAO 8-4

- **i.** Additional nominations may be submitted either (1) in writing or (2) electronically, in either case on forms supplied by the Stated Clerk, which shall include consent of the nominee to serve, if elected, and a brief statement regarding the nominee. In the event that a nomination is submitted electronically, the nominator should be aware that responsibility for such nomination rests with the nominator and that non- delivery is the sole responsibility of the nominator. Because the nominator has sole responsibility for delivery of a nomination, the nominator should obtain a receipt verifying successful electronic delivery of the nomination. The nominee is to give consent to only one nomination. In the event that the nominee is nominated for more than one position, the nominee may indicate to which nomination the nominee consents. The deadline for these nominations is the close of the afternoon session of the first day of the Assembly. The Clerk's office shall issue a supplement to the Assembly's Nominating Committee report during the second day's business sessions. No floor nomination will be received unless the nominee's name was previously submitted to the Nominating Committee according to RAO 8-4.d and e, excepting circumstances where there is no nominee from the Nominating Committee.

Adopted by Northern New England Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 2, 2019 Attested by TE C.S. Per Almquist, stated clerk

6For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: “More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime" (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online athttp://www.cdc.gov/ violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf).

- **(3)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(4)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(5)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with Southern New England Presbytery committed to offer $3,000; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly.

OVERTURE 14 from Southern New England Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 14-1.10, 14-1.11, and 14-1.12 to Allow Non-ordained Persons to serve on Committees and Boards" (Version 2)

Whereas, vigorous participation of women in the life of the early church is attested by the New Testament: they helped select (Acts 1:14) and train (Acts 18:26) leaders of the church, were prophets (Acts 21:8-9), served the church through deeds of mercy in vital ways (Acts 9:36–41), were instrumental in the planting of churches (Acts 16:12–15; 17:4,12) and other missionary endeavors (Acts 18:1f), and were acknowledged as important leaders for the church (Rom. 16:3-4); and Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America believes Christ has called his church to be a “spiritual commonwealth” (BCO 3-1), in which members elect godly men to be ordained as elders who are given the power of jurisdiction as they act jointly in the courts of the church (BCO 3-2); and Whereas, a robustly complementarian perspective affirms the oversight of these elders and the proper, vital and full expression of the gifts given by Christ to men and women for his service; and 619

<a id="ga47-p622"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=622 printed_page=620 -->

Whereas, as part of the calling of church leaders to “equip the saints for the  
work of ministry for building up the body of Christ" (Eph. 4:12),  
sessions throughout the PCA identify gifted men and women to serve on  
committees of the church, such as missions, building, and pastoral search  
committees; and  
Whereas, in contrast with a commission in the PCA, which is "authorized  
to deliberate and conclude the business referred to it," committees are  
appointed by courts "to examine, consider and report" to their  
constituting court concerning the matters that court delegates to them  
(BCO 15-1) and thus do not exercise governing authority; and  
Whereas, in accordance with this principle, Permanent Committees  
established by the General Assembly are “to serve and not to direct any  
Church judicatories. They are not to establish policy, but rather execute  
policy established by the General Assembly" (BCO 14-1.7); and  
Whereas, these considerations suggest there is no impediment to an  
unordained member in good standing in the PCA serving on a Permanent  
Committee or Agency of the General Assembly established in BCO 14-  
1.12; and  
Whereas, the 45th General Assembly adopted the recommendation of The  
Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church  
that stated "sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly strive to  
develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom  
of godly women in the local, regional, and national church, and  
particularly consider overtures that would allow qualified women to  
serve on appropriate committees and agencies within the church"; and  
Whereas, the 46th General Assembly answered in the negative an overture  
to allow non- ordained members on General Assembly Agency Boards  
on the grounds that BCO 14-1.11 had to be amended prior to amendment  
of the PCA Bylaws, which governs the Agencies;  
Therefore be it resolved to amend The Book of Church Order by deleting  
14-1.10; by amending 14-1.11 as follows (and renumbering as 14-1.10);  
by adding a new 14-1.11; and by amending 14-1.12 as follows:

OVERTURE 15 from West Hudson Presbytery

### (CCB, OC)

“Amend RAO 11-5 to Prevent Confusion and Possible Contradictory Actions on Overtures by Multiple Committees of Commissioners"

Whereas, Presbyteries (ordinarily) and other bodies (in some circumstances) request action by the General Assembly on specific matters by means of an Overture (RAO 11-4); Whereas, an Overture may contain subject matter that could appear pertinent to more than one Committee of Commissioners; Whereas, currently RAO 11-5 states that “the Stated Clerk shall refer all overtures requesting amendment of the Book of Church Order or the Rules of Assembly Operations to the Committee on Constitutional Business for its advice to the Overtures Committee"; Whereas, the term “shall" in the BCO delineates an obligatory rather than a permissible action, requiring the Stated Clerk to refer such overtures to the Committee on Constitutional Business, which then shall forward such overtures (along with CCB's advice) to the Overtures Committee; Whereas, if an Overture requesting amendment to the BCO or the RAO was also referred to another Committee of Commissioners (CoC), the result could be confusion as to which Committee's recommendation, whether Overtures or another CoC, should be taken up by the Assembly; and Whereas, it is possible that in such instance contradictory recommendations could be brought to the Assembly by two (or more) CoCs; Therefore, be it resolved, that the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America amend RAO 11-5 with the following additions (additions are underlined):

11-5. Upon receipt the Stated Clerk shall refer all overtures requesting amendment of the Book of Church Order or the Rules of Assembly Operations to the Committee on Constitutional Business for its advice to the Overtures Committee. Upon receipt, the Stated Clerk shall forward all overtures concerning presbytery boundaries or a new presbytery to the permanent Committee on Mission to North America. Any overture, other than an overture proposing amendment to the Constitution (which shall be referred to the Committee on Constitutional Business for its advice to the Overtures Committee), having to do with the nature or responsibilities of a permanent Committee or Agency shall be referred by the Clerk to the appropriate permanent Committee or Agency or ad interim committee. All other overtures shall be referred to 626

<a id="ga47-p629"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=629 printed_page=627 -->

## APPENDIX V

the Overtures Committee. No overture shall be referred for consideration and recommendation to more than one Committee of Commissioners, permanent Committee or Agency or ad interim committee; an overture, however, may be referred for informational purposes only to another Committee of Commissioners, permanent Committee or Agency or ad interim committee. All overtures shall be published in the Commissioner Handbook with reference for consideration indicated.

Adopted by West Hudson Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 7, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Christopher M. Diebold, stated clerk

OVERTURE 16 from Georgia Foothills Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend the RAO to Provide for a Moderator-Elect and Vice-Moderator by Revision of RAO 1-4, Addition of RAO 1-6, 1-7, and 1-8, and Revision of RAO 2-1, 2-3"

Whereas, the role of Moderator of the General Assembly is a complicated responsibility. It will be helpful for a man to have a year's notice in order to prepare for his duties, and Whereas, some PCA presbyteries have a Moderator-In-Nomination rule in their Standing Rules, and Whereas, other Presbyterian denominations, such as the Associate Reformed Presbyterian Church and the Evangelical Presbyterian Church elect a Moderator-Elect or Vice-Moderator, and Whereas, the Assembly subsequent to the election of a Moderator-Elect or Vice-Moderator still would have the option of electing another man as Moderator, and Whereas, since we use electronic voting rather than voting cards or paper ballots, it is no longer necessary to specify that paper ballots be used, and Whereas, it is customary that the Moderator yield the chair at times. The revision to RAO 2-1 specifies who the Moderator pro tempore may be, and Whereas, under Robert's Rules of Order the term “privileges of the floor" only means that one is allowed to be present during a meeting and does not mean that one has the right to speak (RONR [11th ed.] p. 29, footnote). The original purpose of RAO 2-3 was to give a former Moderator of the General Assembly the right to participate in debate. One must be a commissioner in order to vote.

627

<a id="ga47-p630"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=630 printed_page=628 -->

Therefore, be it resolved that Georgia Foothills Presbytery overtures the Forty-seventh General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to amend the Rules of Assembly Operations by revision of RAO 1-4; by addition of RAO 1-6, 1-7, and 1-8; and by revision of RAO 2-1, 2-3 to provide for a Moderator-Elect and a Vice-Moderator as follows:

### ARTICLE I. ORGANIZATION OF A GENERAL

### ASSEMBLY'S MEETING

1-4. If more than one commissioner is nominated, election shall be by secret ballot, <del>on ballots provided by the Stated</del> <del>Clerk</del>. <del>Tellers appointed by the Stated Clerk shall gather and</del> <del>count the ballots, and report the tabulation to the Stated Clerk</del>. If no nominee receives a majority of the votes cast, a second ballot shall be called on the two nominees who received the highest number of votes on the first ballot. The Moderator shall declare an election when a nominee receives a majority of the votes cast by the commissioners present and voting.

1-5. No change.

1-6. After the Moderator has been elected, he shall preside over the election of a Moderator-elect. There shall be only one nominating speech not to exceed five minutes for each nominee. No seconding speeches shall be permitted. 1-7. If more than one commissioner is nominated, election shall be by secret ballot. If no nominee receives a majority of the votes cast, a second ballot shall be called on the two nominees who received the highest number of votes on the first ballot. The Moderator shall declare an election when a nominee receives a majority of the votes cast by the commissioners present and voting.

1-8. The Moderator-Elect shall be placed in nomination for Moderator at the subsequent General Assembly. Additional nominations may be made from the floor.

### ARTICLE II. THE MODERATOR

2-1. The Moderator shall preside at all sessions of the Assembly except when he may invite the Moderator-Elect (Vice-Moderator), a former Moderator, or another commissioner to act temporarily as the presiding officer.

628

<a id="ga47-p631"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=631 printed_page=629 -->

### 2-2.No change.

2-3. Any former Moderator attending a General Assembly shall have the privileges of the floor, may participate in debate, and, if he is a commissioner, may vote.

Approved by Georgia Foothills Presbytery at its stated meeting, January 26, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Don Aldin, stated clerk

OVERTURE 17 from Houston Metro Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 32-8 to Allow for Video Testimony by Witnesses”

Whereas, an important aspect of any case of process is the gathering and  
presenting of evidence, including testimony produced by witnesses;  
Whereas, testimony by witnesses before the court can be inconvenient due  
to geographic distance or other circumstances;  
Whereas, it is important that witnesses be examined with an opportunity to  
be cross-examined by both parties (cf. BCO 32-13); and  
Whereas, technology has made available the possibility of having a virtual  
presence with video and audio interaction even when a person is  
geographically distant from a meeting or court room, and the courts of  
the civil magistrate allow for video testimony by witnesses;  
Therefore, be it resolved, that the General Assembly of the Presbyterian  
Church in America amend BCO 32-8 with the following (additions are  
underlined, deletions are struck through):

32-8. When the offense with which an accused person stands  
charged took place at a distance, <del>and</del> or it is inconvenient for  
the witnesses to appear before the court having jurisdiction,  
that court may either (a) appoint a commission of its body, or  
(b) request the coordinate court contiguous to the place where  
the facts occurred, to take the testimony for it, or (c) have the  
testimony taken by videoconference, which shall employ  
technical means that ensure that all persons participating in the  
meeting can see and hear each other at the same time, and  
which allows for live cross-examination by both parties. The  
accused shall always have reasonable notice of the time and  
place of the meeting of this commission or coordinate court.

Adopted by Houston Metro Presbytery at its stated meeting, January 18, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Lou Veiga, stated clerk

<a id="ga47-p632"></a>

OVERTURE 20 from Nashville Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Establish Study Committee on Domestic Abuse," (Version 4)

Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25- 27; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are "against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society;7 and

7 For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: "More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime" (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering 637

<a id="ga47-p640"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=640 printed_page=638 -->

Whereas, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and Whereas, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; Therefore, be it resolved that Nashville Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault;

- **(2)** the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins;

- **(3)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(4)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(5)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and

statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online at http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl -2009-a.pdf). 638

<a id="ga47-p641"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=641 printed_page=639 -->

## APPENDIX V

Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with General Assembly appealing to the various Presbyteries to fund this initiative via such gifts. Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly.

Adopted by Nashville Presbytery at its stated meeting, November 13, 2018 Attested by /s/ TE R. Neil Spence, stated clerk

OVERTURE 21 from Nashville Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend Book of Church Order 14-1.10., 14-1.11., and 14-1.12” (Version 3)

Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America believes Christ has called his  
church to be a “spiritual commonwealth” (BCO 3-1), in which members  
elect godly men to be ordained as elders who are given the power of  
jurisdiction as they act jointly in the courts of the church (BCO 3-2); and  
Whereas, a robustly complementarian perspective affirms the oversight of  
these elders and the proper, vital and full expression of the gifts given by  
Christ to men and women for his service; and  
Whereas ereas, vigorous participation of women in the life of the early  
church is attested by the New Testament: they helped select (Acts 1:14)  
and train (Acts 18:26) leaders of the church, prophesied (Acts 21:8-9),  
served the church through deeds of mercy in vital ways (Acts 9:36–41),  
were instrumental in the planting of churches (Acts 16:12–15; 17:4,12)  
and other missionary endeavors (Acts 18:1f), and were acknowledged as  
important leaders for the church (Rom. 16:3-4); and  
Whereas, as part of the calling of church leaders to “equip the saints for the  
work of ministry for building up the body of Christ" (Eph. 4:12), sessions  
throughout the PCA identify gifted men and women to serve on  
committees of the church, such as missions, building, and pastoral search  
committees; and  
Whereas, in contrast with a commission in the PCA, which is "authorized to  
deliberate and conclude the business referred to it," committees are  
appointed by courts "to examine, consider and report" to their  
constituting court concerning the matters that court delegates to them  
(BCO 15-1) and thus do not exercise governing authority; and

639

OVERTURE 22 from Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (to OC) “Urge Assembly to Adopt Overture 4 Regarding Nashville Statement”

Be it resolved that Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery requests the 2019 PCA General Assembly to adopt Overture 4 from Calvary Presbytery: “Declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's ‘Nashville Statement’ on Biblical Sexuality as a Biblically Faithful Declaration" (Exhibit A, attached).

Adopted by Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 23, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE Paul Rich, stated clerk

### EXHIBIT A

OVERTURE 4 from Calvary Presbytery (to OC) “Declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's ‘Nashville Statement' on Biblical Sexuality as a Biblically Faithful Declaration"

Whereas the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's "Nashville Statement" declares:

645

<a id="ga47-p648"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=648 printed_page=646 -->

Article 1 WE AFFIRM that God has designed marriage to be a covenantal, sexual, procreative, lifelong union of one man and one woman, as husband and wife, and is meant to signify the covenant love between Christ and his bride the church. WE DENY that God has designed marriage to be a homosexual, polygamous, or polyamorous relationship. We also deny that marriage is a mere human contract rather than a covenant made before God. Article 2 WE AFFIRM that God's revealed will for all people is chastity outside of marriage and fidelity within marriage. WE DENY that any affections, desires, or commitments ever justify sexual intercourse before or outside marriage; nor do they justify any form of sexual immorality. Article 3 WE AFFIRM that God created Adam and Eve, the first human beings, in his own image, equal before God as persons, and distinct as male and female. WE DENY that the divinely ordained differences between male and female render them unequal in dignity or worth. Article 4 WE AFFIRM that divinely ordained differences between male and female reflect God's original creation design and are meant for human good and human flourishing. WE DENY that such differences are a result of the Fall or are a tragedy to be overcome. Article 5 WE AFFIRM that the differences between male and female reproductive structures are integral to God's design for selfconception as male or female. WE DENY that physical anomalies or psychological conditions nullify the God-appointed link between biological sex and self-conception as male or female. Article 6 WE AFFIRM that those born with a physical disorder of sex development are created in the image of God and have dignity and worth equal to all other image-bearers. They are acknowledged by our Lord Jesus in his words about “eunuchs who were born that way from their mother's womb." With all others they are welcome as faithful followers of Jesus Christ and should embrace their biological sex insofar as it may be known. 646

<a id="ga47-p649"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=649 printed_page=647 -->

## APPENDIX V

WE DENY that ambiguities related to a person's biological sex render one incapable of living a fruitful life in joyful obedience to Christ. Article 7 WE AFFIRM that self-conception as male or female should be defined by God's holy purposes in creation and redemption as revealed in Scripture. WE DENY that adopting a homosexual or transgender selfconception is consistent with God's holy purposes in creation and redemption. Article 8 WE AFFIRM that people who experience sexual attraction for the same sex may live a rich and fruitful life pleasing to God through faith in Jesus Christ, as they, like all Christians, walk in purity of life. WE DENY that sexual attraction for the same sex is part of the natural goodness of God's original creation, or that it puts a person outside the hope of the gospel. Article 9 WE AFFIRM that sin distorts sexual desires by directing them away from the marriage covenant and toward sexual immorality— a distortion that includes both heterosexual and homosexual immorality. WE DENY that an enduring pattern of desire for sexual immorality justifies sexually immoral behavior. Article 10 WE AFFIRM that it is sinful to approve of homosexual immorality or transgenderism and that such approval constitutes an essential departure from Christian faithfulness and witness. WE DENY that the approval of homosexual immorality or transgenderism is a matter of moral indifference about which otherwise faithful Christians should agree to disagree. Article 11 WE AFFIRM our duty to speak the truth in love at all times, including when we speak to or about one another as male or female. WE DENY any obligation to speak in such ways that dishonor God's design of his image bearers as male and female. Article 12 WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ gives both merciful pardon and transforming power, and that this pardon

647

<a id="ga47-p650"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=650 printed_page=648 -->

and power enable a follower of Jesus to put to death sinful desires and to walk in a manner worthy of the Lord. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ is insufficient to forgive all sexual sins and to give power for holiness to every believer who feels drawn into sexual sin. Article 13 WE AFFIRM that the grace of God in Christ enables sinners to forsake transgender self- conceptions and by divine forbearance to accept the God-ordained link between one's biological sex and one's self-conception as male or female. WE DENY that the grace of God in Christ sanctions selfconceptions that are at odds with God's revealed will. Article 14 WE AFFIRM that Christ Jesus has come into the world to save sinners and that through Christ's death and resurrection forgiveness of sins and eternal life are available to every person who repents of sin and trusts in Christ alone as Savior, WE DENY that the Lord's arm is too short to save or that any sinner is beyond his reach.

Therefore be it resolved that the Calvary Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly and asks it to declare the Council on Biblical Manhood & Womanhood's "Nashville Statement" on biblical sexuality as a biblically faithful declaration and refer the “Nashville Statement" to the Committee on Discipleship Ministries for inclusion and promotion among its denominational teaching materials.

Grounds: “The Nashville Statement," carefully worked out by the Council on Biblical Manhood and Womanhood in 2017, is a timely statement that speaks into the current confusion surrounding gender and sexuality within the evangelical church (including the PCA) and the broader culture. Signed by many leaders within the Reformed and evangelical world, it is a balanced and biblically faithful attempt to "speak the truth in love" (Eph. 4:15) on one of the most pivotal and controversial issues facing the church today. Additionally, “The Nashville Statement” clearly reiterates the truth of foundational passages of Scripture and our confessional understanding of marriage, gender, and sexual ethics. It affirms God's good purpose in ordaining the binary nature of gender while bestowing His image on mankind (Gen. 1:27), His design for marriage between one biological man and one biological woman (Gen. 1:23, 24), and the sinfulness of homosexual and transgender desire as well as conduct (Mat. 15:18, 19; I Cor. 6:9-11). In 648

<a id="ga47-p651"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=651 printed_page=649 -->

## APPENDIX V

addition to affirming these historic, orthodox truths, the Nashville Statement also lifts up the hope of the gospel to the sexual struggler, pointing the reader to our Lord Jesus Christ as “the double cure," saving us both from sin's guilt and power. Therefore, the PCA would do well to commend “The Nashville Statement" and prepare it for distribution through Committee on Discipleship Ministries. Adopted by Calvary Presbytery at its stated meeting, October 25, 2018. Attested by /s/ RE Melton L. Duncan, stated clerk

OVERTURE 23 from Central Carolina Presbytery (to IRC) “Withdraw from the National Association of Evangelicals”
