OVERTURE 24 from Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery (to AC, CDM, “Add Constitutional Precedence Statement to

### MNA, MTW, RUF

Policy Manuals"(Revised)

### CC, CTS, PCAF, PCA-RBI, RH)

[Note: An earlier version of this overture appeared online in early March. At its May 4 meeting Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery revised the first “Whereas” clause to clarify the Committees and Agencies involved. There is no other change to the original overture.] Whereas the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) currently has five Permanent Committees (Administrative Committee, Committee on Discipleship Ministries, Mission to North America, Mission to the World, and Reformed University Fellowship) and five Agencies (Covenant College, Covenant Seminary, PCA Foundation, PCA Retirement & Benefits, Inc., and Ridge Haven), and may in the future have other or additional Permanent Committees and Agencies (all such current and future Permanent Committees and Agencies, collectively, the “Permanent Committees and Agencies”) [BCO 14.1.12; RAO 14.1]; and Whereas it is necessary for the Permanent Committees and Agencies to function at all times under the authority of the Constitution (as defined in BCO Preface III, and which includes the Westminster Confession of Faith, the Larger Catechism and Shorter Catechism, and the Book of Church Order, collectively, the “Constitution”); [BCO 14.1.7–8; 14.6; Article V.G of the Corporate Bylaws]; and Whereas it is standard operating procedure for organizations to write policy manuals; and Whereas the Permanent Committees and Agencies rightly and necessarily have at times produced their respective policy manuals; and Whereas it is essential for every policy manual of the Permanent Committees and Agencies to remain subject to the Constitution; and Whereas it is possible for unanticipated conflicts, potential conflicts, or ambiguities to arise between Permanent Committee and Agency policy manuals and the Constitution; and

651

<a id="ga47-p654"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=654 printed_page=652 -->

Whereas it is a well-recognized best practice for policy manuals of organizations to explicitly state their subordination to organizational constitutional documents and by-laws; Therefore, it is resolved that the Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly to add the following statement to the preface of all policy manuals of the Permanent Committees and Agencies: "At every point, this entire manual is subordinate to the entire Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America—the Westminster Standards and the Book of Church Order. If there exists any conflict between the PCA's constitutional documents and the content and stipulations of this manual, the Constitution carries final authority." Further resolved, that any policy manual produced or amended by any of the Permanent Committees and Agencies shall, before becoming operational, be approved by its respective board and submitted to the General Assembly for ratification through the usual process of the reports of the Permanent Committees and Agencies. Further resolved, that each of the Permanent Committees and Agencies report back on the implementation of these actions to their respective Committee of Commissioners at the 48th General Assembly.

Rationale: In order to carry out their responsibilities faithfully, Permanent Committees and Agencies must be able to develop and propose policies to the General Assembly for ratification. BCO 14.1.7 indicates that "The Assembly's committees are to serve and not to direct any Church judicatories. They are not to establish policy, but rather execute policy established by the General Assembly." The only effective method to ensure Permanent Committee and Agency policies yield to the PCA constitution, and the only way to ensure that constitutional due process for staff of these permanent Committees and Agencies in relation to written policies, is (1) to give the PCA constitution explicitly stated priority in all policy manuals, and (2) to make policy changes according to BCO 14.1.7, which grants the General Assembly full visibility into proposed policies (and any wording changes to policies) in order to exercise its constitutionally-appointed powers of ratification.

The action of the 5th General Assembly, for example, delivers a clear process in relation to the Committee on Mission to the World (CMTW). This GA action (1977, p. 72, 5–64, IV, 9) differentiated between the MTW policy manual and the MTW handbook, when it determined "the policy manual to be revised only by General Assembly procedures while changes in the handbooks (which unavoidably need continual changes to meet changing 652

<a id="ga47-p655"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=655 printed_page=653 -->

## APPENDIX V

situations with regard to such things as insurance, annuity, travel, etc.) be reported annually to the MTW Committee of Commissioners (CoC) at the General Assembly for their approval." Usual process for policy changes then requires that changes/additions be submitted by CMTW to the CoC for ratification by the General Assembly, with a CMTW minute to this effect in each instance. The CoC should then include these as recommendations in their report to GA (including any minority reports).

In 2014, the 42nd General Assembly of the PCA passed Overture 6, “Child Protection in the PCA." This overture directed the Permanent Agencies and Committees “to review their policies, procedures and practices in the area of child protection, including their response to child sexual abuse disclosures, their faithfulness in reporting child sexual abuse to duly appointed proper representatives of the God-ordained civil authorities, in accordance with local laws, their care for survivors of child sexual abuse, and their future plans to help educate the PCA on child sexual abuse, and all other areas of response consistent with Scripture and the Constitution of the PCA and report to the 43rd General Assembly through the Administrative Committee, after it has referred the matter to and received a report from the Cooperative Ministries Committee." We trust that the Permanent Agencies and Committees have attended to these Overture 6 mandates, but to date no such policies or revisions to policy manuals have been reviewed by the General Assembly. A more recent example appeared in 2018, when MTW created and implemented a sexual harassment policy, which has yet to receive General Assembly ratification.

Adopted by Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery at its stated meeting, February 23, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE Paul Rich, stated clerk Revision adopted by Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery, May 4, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE Paul Rich, stated clerk

OVERTURE 25 from the Suncoast Florida Presbytery (to CDM) “Support Christian Education”

Whereas the Presbyterian Church in America has seen fit to establish Covenant College and Covenant Theological Seminary to educate students in accordance with a Biblical worldview, including studies in covenantal and Reformed theology, as well as studies touching upon our Lord's Great Commission and the extension of His Kingdom; and 653

<a id="ga47-p656"></a>

Whereas the Scriptures command faithful Biblical instruction be given to God's covenant children as well, those little ones being brought up in the context of God's covenant people and in accordance with their union with Christ (Deut 6:7-15; Prov. 22:6; Mt. 19:14, 15; Eph. 6:4), making a distinction between their education and that of unbelievers; and Whereas the wisdom of God being expressed through His people reveals itself to be "pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, and sincere..." (James 3:17); and Whereas a considerable number of parents in our churches, increasing in their knowledge of God's Word and works (Ps. 78:4-7), desire an educational context for their covenant children consistent with God's Word, a context which encourages them to rejoice in Him as Creator, Redeemer, and Lord over all; a context which encourages them to exercise dominion as His image-bearers for His honor, one which will enable them to be informed by and conformed to His Truth (John 17:17); and Whereas a considerable number of materialistic/secular world view ideas (such as those touching upon gender identity issues, new definitions of marriage and family, sexual boundaries, questions of who has ultimate authority over the children, etc.) become increasingly politicized and passed into law; and Whereas Christian families are experiencing an increase of tension in the public school arena as school policies, approved practices, classroom instruction, discussion, and textbooks oppose and in some instances, vilify, their Biblical convictions; indeed, sometimes resulting in legal action on the part of the state (more recently in reference to gender identity issues); and Whereas parents of baptized children make vows to bring the child up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord (BCO 56-5); and Whereas the congregation also makes a vow to assist these parents in the aforesaid endeavor (BCO 56-5); and Whereas the elders and deacons of Christ's church work together in promoting the spiritual well-being of church members (including the covenant children) encouraging, praying, and supporting if necessary (and possible) what tends to their spiritual growth and good. (BCO 6-1,

### 3; BCO 7-2; BCO 8-3; BCO 9-1; BCO 12-5);

Therefore be it resolved that the Presbyteries, Sessions, and Diaconates of the Presbyterian Church in America, be encouraged to embrace and provide a supportive posture for Christian education in our churches and communities by:

- **a.** Teaching on the nature, purpose, and tasks involved in bringing covenant children up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord (Ephesians 6:4).

- **C.** Considering/dialoguing with members in our covenant communities regarding the privileges and benefits of a wholly Christian education in which the primary goal is the development of a mind and heart consistently conformed to the worldview of the Bible as it touches upon all aspects of living in union with Christ- in God's amazing world under Christ's reign (Genesis 1:1; Psalm 2:6, 11, 12; Psalm 19:1; Psalm 24; Romans 12:1, 2). By offering, whenever possible, financial, spiritual and instructional assistance helpful to those families expressing a desire to pursue a wholly Christian education for their children.

OVERTURE 26 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Establish Study Committee on Domestic Abuse” (Version 5)

Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25- 27; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are “against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society; and Whereas, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and

655

<a id="ga47-p658"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=658 printed_page=656 -->

Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and Whereas, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; Therefore, be it resolved to hereby overture the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault;

- **(2)** pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins;

- **(3)** pastoral resources available on the perpetrators of these sins;

- **(4)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(5)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(6)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly. Adopted by Tennessee Valley Presbytery at its stated meeting, January 12, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Jacob A. Bennett

OVERTURE 27 from Westminster Presbytery  
(to AC)  
“Study Possibility of Remote Voting at General Assembly"  
Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America was founded as a "grass-  
roots" denomination with power and authority flowing from the bottom  
up; and  
Whereas, the expense of sending a commissioner to the General Assembly  
has become prohibitive for many small churches in the PCA; and  
Whereas, many commissioners would attend the General Assembly, yet are  
unable because of health restrictions; and  
Whereas, the General Assembly meetings now have a small representation  
by ruling elders; and  
Whereas, it is in accordance with the founding principles of the PCA to have  
parity of the teaching and ruling elders in authority; and  
Whereas, it is in accordance with the founding principles of the PCA and  
our BCO to have parity of teaching and ruling elders on General  
Assembly committees (BCO 14-1; Principles for the Organization of the  
Assembly, item 10) and to have at least parity of teaching and ruling  
elders at General Assembly court meetings (BCO 14-2); and  
Whereas, the technology exists to have commissioners vote on issues of the  
General Assembly from a distance while they watch the proceedings of  
the General Assembly online; and  
Whereas, the General Assembly as presently structured would continue with  
the exception of a distance voting commissioner;  
Therefore, Westminster Presbytery overtures the 47th General Assembly to  
instruct the PCA Administrative Committee to investigate and report at  
the 48th General Assembly a plan to create a DVC (Distance Voting  
Commissioner) which would entail the ability of regularly elected  
commissioners to vote electronically at a distance from the site of the  
General Assembly.  
Adopted by Westminster Presbytery at its stated meeting, March 9, 2019

OVERTURE 28 from Westminster Presbytery (to OC) “Affirmations and Denials regarding Homosexuality”

Whereas a controversy has arisen in the Presbyterian Church in America over certain teachings espoused by Revoice, an organization that is promoting LGBT+ flourishing in various PCA churches, it has become necessary to clarify and reaffirm what the Bible teaches concerning homosexuality and gender; 657

<a id="ga47-p660"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=660 printed_page=658 -->

Therefore be it resolved that Westminster Presbytery ask the 47th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to adopt the following 12 articles that clarify and affirm the Bible's teaching about homosexuality and gender. Article 1 WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction, homosexual orientation, and homosexual acts are against nature and sinful. (Rom. 1:26-27) WE DENY that homosexual attraction is part of the original creation order, since God created man in His image male and female for one another. (Gen. 1:27-28; Gen. 2:18, 21-24; Mt. 19:4-6) Article 2 WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction is a vile, degrading, and dishonorable passion, and those who condone homosexuality invite the further judgment of God. (Rom. 1:26-32) WE DENY that unrepentant homosexuals will inherit the kingdom of God. (1 Cor. 6:9-10) Article 3 WE AFFIRM that Jesus condemned both sinful sexual attractions and sinful sexual actions. (Mt. 5:27-28) WE DENY that scripture permits homosexual attraction and orientation. (Rom. 1:26-27) Article 4 WE AFFIRM that those with homosexual attractions, incestuous attractions, and bestial attractions are "sexual minorities" in the church. WE DENY that there is any virtue in being identified as a “sexual minority," because all of these dispositions are sinful. (Lev. 18:6, 22-23; 20:13, 15-16) Article 5 WE AFFIRM that God by His grace can change an unnatural sexual orientation. (1 Cor. 6:11; 1 Jn. 1:9) WE DENY that unnatural sexual orientations are fixed, permanent, and unchangeable. (Col. 1:21-23) Article 6 WE AFFIRM that many people having a homosexual orientation do not desire this orientation. WE DENY that unwanted vile passions are natural, neutral, or good. (Rom. 7:21-25) Article 7 WE AFFIRM that Christians ought to abhor homosexual sin (Lev. 18:22). Abhorrence of all sin should be cultivated. Those who love the Lord hate evil. (Ps. 97:10) WE DENY that revulsion and abhorrence of homosexual sin is sinful. (Rom. 12:9; 1 Cor. 13:4-7)

658

<a id="ga47-p661"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=661 printed_page=659 -->

## APPENDIX V

Article 8 WE AFFIRM that people living in homosexual sin should be shown kindness and lovingly encouraged to turn from their sin to serve Christ who alone can deliver them from sin and its shame. (Mk. 2:16-17; James 5:19-20) WE DENY that it is loving or kind to try to diminish or remove the shame of homosexual attraction and orientation, since God calls it shameful. (Rom. 1:26-27; Jer. 6:14-15) Article 9 WE AFFIRM that repentant sinners turning from all unnatural attractions and trusting in Christ should be welcomed into the church as members in good standing. (1 Tim. 1:15-16) WE DENY that followers of Christ who struggle with homosexual attraction should be identified as “LGBT+ Christians," because it dishonors Christ to identify with sinful attractions and orientations. (2 Cor. 5:16-17; 1 Cor. 6:9- 11) Article 10 WE AFFIRM that homosexual attraction should be mortified by the power of the Spirit. (Col. 3:1-7; Rom. 8:12-14; 1 Thess. 4:3-5) WE DENY that continuing homosexual attraction or failure to attain orientation change is evidence of God's approval of these unnatural and vile passions. (Rom. 7:21-25; Rom. 1:26-27) Article 11 WE AFFIRM that those struggling with unlawful sexual attractions of any kind should be encouraged to seek the help, prayer, and counsel of mature believers, elders, and pastors. (James 5:16; Heb. 3:12-13; Heb. 10:24-25) WE DENY that those struggling with homosexual attraction and orientation should suffer in silence. (Gal. 6:1-2) Article 12 WE AFFIRM that our inward self-conception and outward gender identity must conform to the sex God assigned us at conception, and thus we are to live in obedience to his call evident in our reproductive organs. (Dt. 22:5) WE DENY that physical anomalies or psychological conditions nullify the union God has decreed between biological sex and self-conception and gender identity. OVERTURE 31 from Eastern Pennsylvania Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Form an Ad Interim Committee to Address Matters Related to Domestic Abuse, Domestic Oppression, and Sexual Assault" (Version 6) Be it resolved:

- **a.** Prepare an annotated bibliography of recommended pastoral resources available on the nature of domestic abuse, domestic oppression,15 and sexual assault, as well as pastoral resources for the care of victims of these sins;

- **b.** Explore these matters from an historical perspective, giving special consideration of how they have been conceived of and addressed within the Reformed tradition and provide a summary of their findings.

- **C.** Describe "best practices" and policy guidelines that could be helpful for elders, Sessions, Presbyteries, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **d.** If the Committee deems it prudent, it may include in the report any revisions or additions to BCO Rules of Discipline that might more appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process, which changes may be issued as an overture to a subsequent General Assembly by any Presbytery that would wish to do so;

- **a.** These members shall be PCA ministers or PCA ruling elders, and the Committee shall include at least two of each. (Presbyteries, Sessions, and individuals may contact the Moderator with suggested names.)

Rationale:

1. The sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden by Scripture and the Westminster Standards. (For example, see 2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25-27; also, WLC 135 and 139.)

2. These sins are especially heinous as they are “against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151).

3. Sadly, these sins are prevalent in our society, and in the church.16

4. These sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22).

5. It is the responsibility of the elders of the Church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins, with an aim toward a full repentance.

6. These sins have been a concern and a subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly.

7. In 2014, the 42nd General Assembly (Houston, TX) exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children.

8. Many PCA ministers, ruling elders, and candidates report a desire to be resourced in order to provide better pastoral care on these sins and their resulting complex consequences.

9. Many PCA ministers, ruling elders, and candidates report a desire to learn of "best practices" regarding church and presbytery policies in this area. For example, some ministers and elders are unaware of the different levels of background checks that can be utilized in screening. Some do not know what their State's laws are regarding mandatory reporters or in what situations those laws may or may not apply.

10. Our BCO Part II Rules of Discipline might benefit from additions or revisions that address these matters. For example, the following BCO provisions might benefit from review and revision, at least in the context of a minor who accuses an adult of sexual misconduct: BCO 35-1....The accused party may be allowed, but shall not be compelled to testify; but the accuser shall be required to testify, on the demand of the accused.... BCO 32-13. In order that the trial may be fair and impartial, the witnesses shall be examined in the presence of the accused, or at least after he shall have received due citation to attend. Witnesses may be cross-examined by both parties, and any questions asked must be pertinent to the issue. BCO 32-20. Process, in case of scandal, shall commence within the space of one year after the offense was committed, unless it has recently become flagrant.... BCO 35-4. No witness afterwards to be examined, unless a member of the court, shall be present during the examination of another witness on the same case, if either party object.

11. Reporting Recommendations through the Overtures Committee In the past, Ad Interim Committees have customarily reported recommendations directly to the GA floor. But going through the OC is a more prudent and efficient path for any AIC recommendations on BCO changes and/or any recommended statement for GA adoption. Furthermore, RAO 12-1 stipulates "all recommendations proposing amendment to the Constitution shall be referred to the Overtures Committee for their review and recommendation to the General Assembly." And this would also be the most prudent and efficient path for any BCO recommendation from this AIC.

663

<a id="ga47-p666"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=666 printed_page=664 -->

The RAO section on OC reports to GA provides a wiser method for handling all recommendations from the AIC:

RAO 15-8.c. "A recommendation [from the OC] shall be considered under the standard rules governing debate, but Subsidiary Motions (RRO VI) to Postpone Indefinitely, to Amend, to Commit, and to Limit Debate; and Incidental Motions (RRO VIII) to Divide a Question, to Consider Seriatim, and Constitutional Inquiries, shall not be permitted. A motion to Recommit shall be permitted, but a motion to Recommit With Instructions shall not be permitted." If the 2019 Dallas GA Overtures Committee, and then the Dallas GA, want recommendations from this particular AIC to go through the 2020 Birmingham OC first, that is certainly the constitutional prerogative of the commissioners in Dallas.

Adopted by Eastern Pennsylvania Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 9, 2019 Attested by TE Mel Farrar, stated clerk

OVERTURE 33 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 57-5 to Add Vow Regarding Trinity"

Whereas, there is but one only, living, and true God, who exists as three persons—God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit—of one substance, power, and eternity (WCF 2; WLC 9; WSC 6); and

670

<a id="ga47-p673"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=673 printed_page=671 -->

## APPENDIX V

Whereas, the doctrine of the Trinity is foundational, essential, and vital to the Christian faith; indeed, presbyteries have been instructed to give due and serious consideration to "Appendix W," which includes the affirmation: "the confession of the Trinity is the heartbeat of the Christian religion" (as adopted by the 45th General Assembly, Minutes, 29 and 624); and Whereas, the visible church is made up of those who profess faith in the Lord Jesus Christ (BCO 2-1), and such profession of faith is a profession of the whole Christ, who is both truly God and truly man; and Whereas, we live in a pluralistic age, where there is confusion over the essential being of God, illustrated by the fact that the vast majority of self-professing evangelicals in America affirm that “Jesus is the first and greatest being created by God" (Ligonier Ministries and LifeWay Research, “The State of Theology" 2018); and Whereas, the doctrine of the Trinity has been and is currently under assault by the unbelieving world, by cults, by unitarians, and by various religions; and Whereas, Mormons, Jehovah's Witnesses, and other non-Christian faiths could affirm our current membership vows as stated; and Whereas, the organization of a particular church in the Presbyterian Church in America includes the pronouncement and declaration of its organization in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit (BCO 5-8); and Whereas, when unbaptized persons apply for admission into the Church, they shall make a public profession of their faith, in the presence of the congregation, and thereupon be baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit (BCO 56-6; 57-3), as shall the children of believing parents; and Whereas, "every Christian Church, or union or association of particular churches, is entitled to declare the terms of admission into its communion and the qualifications of its ministers and members" (Preface to the BCO II.2); and Whereas, at least three fellow NAPARC churches include a membership vow requiring affirmation of the Holy Trinity; and Whereas, the current membership vows of the Presbyterian Church in America reference “God" (BCO 57-5), but do not require faith in God as He exists in three persons; Therefore, be it resolved to amend the Book of Church Order 57-5 by adding the following question to the membership vows [as question 2, thereby renumbering questions 2–5 as questions 3–6]:

671

<a id="ga47-p674"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=674 printed_page=672 -->

2. Do you believe in the one, true, and living God who exists in three persons—God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit—who are of the same substance, equal in power and glory?

So that the membership vows in Book of Church Order 57-5 would read:

1. Do you acknowledge yourselves to be sinners in the sight of God, justly deserving His displeasure, and without hope save in His sovereign mercy?

2. Do you believe in the one, true, and living God who exists in three persons—God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Spirit—who are of the same substance, equal in power and glory? 2.3. Do you believe in the Lord Jesus Christ as the Son of God, and Savior of sinners, and do you receive and rest upon Him alone for salvation as He is offered in the Gospel? 3.4. Do you now resolve and promise, in humble reliance upon the grace of the Holy Spirit, that you will endeavor to live as becomes the followers of Christ? 4.5. Do you promise to support the Church in its worship and work to the best of your ability? 5.6. Do you submit yourselves to the government and discipline of the Church, and promise to study its purity and peace?

Adopted by the Tennessee Valley Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 13, 2019 Attested by TE Jacob A. Bennett, stated clerk

process of filing between lower courts and higher courts of the

Whereas, every PCA Presbytery has power “to condemn erroneous opinions which injure the purity and peace of the Church" (BCO 13-9f); and Whereas, the Revoice Conference, held at Memorial Presbyterian Church in St. Louis, Missouri on July 26-28, 2018, was for the purpose of "Supporting, encouraging, and empowering gay, lesbian, same-sex attracted and other LGBT+ Christians;" and Whereas, some within the Presbyterian Church in America are claiming that same-sex attraction is not necessarily a sin but can be a disposition given to some: "that such a disposition of sinful desires are God given for the acceptance of all believers and the Church, and for the promotion of the Glory of God;" or "that individuals with sinful homosexual feelings of same-sex attraction have no control over these feelings and/or attractions; that though they may be unwanted, they are helpless to avoid and are in no need of repentance;" or who answer affirmatively: “Can a person claim to be born with same-sex attraction in the same manner as the man born blind?" or are in agreement with: “I believe my same-sex attractions are broken, but I do not believe they are sinful. It is not sinful for me to be attracted to another man;" or asserting that same-sex attraction and orientation are permissible under the Gospel as long as the person remains celibate; even though these assertions are contrary to what Jesus said that any and all lust in the heart is a sin: “I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart" (Matthew 5:28); and Whereas, the Scripture teaches that same-sex attraction is an evidence that God has given over such people to “the lusts of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them" and “to degrading passions" in which “women exchanged the natural function for that which is unnatural" and "the men abandoned the natural function of the woman and burned in their desire toward one another" because they “exchanged the truth of God for a lie” and “did not see fit to acknowledge God any longer"(Romans 1:24-28); and Whereas, homosexuality is a sin from which God delivered some of the Corinthian Christians (“such were some of you..): “Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived; neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor homosexuals, nor thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers, will inherit the kingdom of God. Such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God"(1 Corinthians 6:9-11); and continues to deliver believers from this and other sins; and

678

<a id="ga47-p681"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=681 printed_page=679 -->

## APPENDIX V

Whereas, same-sex attraction is lust in the very same manner that heterosexual attraction is lust, and both are violations of the seventh commandment as the Larger Catechism teaches: Question 138: What are the duties required in the seventh commandment? Answer: The duties required in the seventh commandment are, chastity in body, mind, affections, words, and behavior; and the preservation of it in ourselves and others; watchfulness over the eyes and all the senses; temperance, keeping of chaste company, modesty in apparel; marriage by those that have not the gift of continency, conjugal love, and cohabitation; diligent labor in our callings; shunning all occasions of uncleanness, and resisting temptations thereunto.

Question 139: What are the sins forbidden in the seventh commandment? Answer: The sins forbidden in the seventh commandment, besides the neglect of the duties required, are, adultery, fornication, rape, incest, sodomy, and all unnatural lusts; all unclean imaginations, thoughts, purposes, and affections; all corrupt or filthy communications, or listening thereunto; wanton looks, impudent or light behavior, immodest apparel; prohibiting of lawful, and dispensing with unlawful marriages; allowing, tolerating, keeping of stews, and resorting to them; entangling vows of single life, undue delay of marriage; having more wives or husbands than one at the same time; unjust divorce, or desertion; idleness, gluttony, drunkenness, unchaste company; lascivious songs, books, pictures, dancings, stage plays; and all other provocations to, or acts of uncleanness, either in ourselves or others. Therefore, be it resolved, that in light of the fact that this current issue is once again confronting the PCA, the 47th General Assembly take the following actions:

That the 47th General Assembly reaffirm the action of the 5th General Assembly:

Whereas God's Word teaches in the Old Testament that homosexuality is a sin, labeling it an “abomination" in such

679

<a id="ga47-p682"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=682 printed_page=680 -->

passages as Leviticus 18:22 and 20:13, and clearly viewing it as sin in the story of Sodom in Genesis 19:1-11; and Whereas the New Testament reaffirms the sinfulness of this “unnatural" practice in such passages as Romans 1:26, 27 and Jude 7, even stating in 1 Corinthians 6:9-11 that homosexuals will not inherit the kingdom of heaven; Therefore, be it resolved that the Fifth General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America affirm the Biblical position for our denomination which states that:

1. The act of homosexuality is a sin according to God's Word;

2. Churches should actively seek to lead the homosexual person to confession and repentance that he might find justification and sanctification in Jesus Christ, according to I Corinthians 6:11; and

3. In light of the Biblical view of its sinfulness, a practicing homosexual continuing in this sin would not be a fit candidate for ordination or membership in the Presbyterian Church in America. (http://pcahistory.org/ga/5th_pcaga_1977.pdf p. 68).

Further, that the 47th General Assembly reaffirm the declaration of the 21st PCA General Assembly:

Therefore, the 21st General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America makes the following declaration: The Bible, which is our infallible rule of faith and practice, commands us to express redemptive love and compassion to all persons. It further commands us to condemn sexual behavior which deviates from God's revealed standard as sinful and destructive. The Bible calls all who engage in these behaviors to repentance by turning to God and proving their repentance by their deeds. The chaplains of the Presbyterian Church in America are committed to providing a compassionate, redemptive, and caring ministry to military service members, their families, and other groups among whom they are called to minister regardless of sexual behavior or the diseases with which their constituents may be afflicted. Therefore, Presbyterian Church in America chaplains endorsed by the Presbyterian and Reformed Joint Commission on Chaplains and

680

<a id="ga47-p683"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=683 printed_page=681 -->

## APPENDIX V

Military Personnel will continue to preach and minister in light of the whole counsel of God on these matters. (http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf pp. 94-95)

And further, that the 47th General Assembly reaffirm the principles regarding the biblical teachings on homosexuality contained in the "A Declaration of Conscience Addressed to the President of the United States of America" adopted by the 21st PCA General Assembly (http://pcahistory.org/ga/21st_pcaga_1993.pdf, pp. 129- 132). The letter said in part:

Mr. President, in this Declaration the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America humbly declares its conscience concerning the moral legitimacy of homosexuality. God has spoken without equivocation through His Word declaring homosexuality to be a perversion of His created order, His moral law, and the foundations of society.... In particular, we feel compelled of conscience to speak because of the slanderous way in which truth has been portrayed, as if opposition to homosexual practice is merely a matter of prejudice against a minority. Please be informed that to act on this basis is to misjudge the issue entirely. This is a question of moral principle, striking at the very root of God's authority, man's created nature, and the structure and preservation of human society. We do not act out of a hateful prejudice which rejects the rights of minority peoples and seeks to exclude them from our communities. On the contrary, we affirm and rejoice in the God-created differences among the peoples of the world and we condemn prejudice as contrary to the heart of the gospel by which we live: that Jesus Christ is by His grace making of various peoples one community of love and fellowship. As His disciples we are called to judge, not by appearances, but to judge righteous judgment (John 7:24). The God we serve has made it plain that with Him there is no partiality, and that in this we must be like Him (Romans 2:11, James 2:1-9). As citizens we support the recognition and protection of the civil rights of all peoples.

681

<a id="ga47-p684"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=684 printed_page=682 -->

And yet in perfect consistency with this commitment we stand resolutely opposed to homosexual practice as incompatible with the temporal good of our nation and the eternal good of its people. As a part of the Church of Jesus Christ, the Presbyterian Church in America has a primary concern for the spiritual well-being of women and men created in the image of God. Responsibility to such a calling will thrust us into irreconcilable conflict with any government policy ostensibly approving a way of life under its sphere of responsibility which is contrary to the eternal good of its citizens. Further, such approval would be a grievous violation of the government's own Godordained calling (Romans 13:1-4).... Together a man and a woman, united outwardly in the institution of marriage, united inwardly in love and affection, and united physically in sexual relations, are the means of transmitting and nurturing life, and that life, growing and flourishing in families, is the necessary foundation of all society. Homosexuality is a violation of these creation ordinances: it is a perversion of human nature, the gift of sexuality and the social order.... Here nature itself, the land personified, is portrayed as revolted by homosexuality as a perversion of God's purposes. Lest this be thought of as an outmoded and unenlightened perspective, the New Testament affirms this same truth with even greater clarity when it excludes, not merely from the land of Israel, but from the eternal Kingdom of God, those who pursue homosexual practice.... Please note: in condemning homosexual practice we claim no self-righteousness. The Bible we cite also teaches that all particular sins flow from one rebellious disposition of heart, a disposition of heart that belongs to all (Ephesians 2:1- 3). If we have been preserved from this perversion, it is only by God's mercy. And that mercy in Jesus Christ is so broad and free that may extend even to those caught up in homosexual practice, freeing them from its bondage. In the same passage we cited above the Apostle reminds the Corinthian believers, "And such were some of you; but you 682

<a id="ga47-p685"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=685 printed_page=683 -->

## APPENDIX V

were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God." To conclude, while condemning homosexual practice, we affirm our duty to love and do good to all, even those who are pursuing this perversion. But for us such love includes the responsibility to speak the truth in love. The truth is that our nation will suffer grievously if accommodated to this perversion. More profoundly, however, the truth is that those given over to homosexual practice will face the judgment of God. We understand the gospel to teach that there is no hope for such persons until they see this truth, embrace it, and turn away from their perversion through the power of Jesus Christ. Thus love requires that we bear witness to their hopeless condition in order that they might find hope. Love forbids our silence in the face of the eternal consequences of believing a lie. And further, that the 47th General Assembly reaffirm the action of the 24th General Assembly: We affirm the Bible's teaching that promotion of homosexual conduct and relationships by any society, including action by the governments to sanction and legitimize homosexual relationships by the legalization of homosexual marriages, is an abominable sin calling for God's judgment upon any such society (Lev. 18:22 and Rom. 1:18-32). We also reaffirm our belief in the transforming power of God's grace and our commitment to 'speaking the truth in love' to those in the homosexual community. (http://pcahistory.org/ga/ 24th_pcaga_1996.pdf, p. 315) And further resolve, to remind all PCA officers and churches:

1. That all persons are born sinners justly deserving God's wrath and condemnation, and that outside of Christ all sinners are enslaved to corruption which distorts their hearts and their understanding of God's created order.

2. That homosexuality is a sin according to God's Word, both in thought, attraction, and behavior.

3. That churches should actively seek to lead all sinners, including those enslaved in homosexuality, to repentance 683

<a id="ga47-p686"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=686 printed_page=684 -->

of their sin and to embrace Jesus Christ by faith as he is offered in the gospel, so they may find justification, sanctification, and their identity in Jesus Christ alone.

4. That long as those enslaved in homosexuality continue in this practice of sin, they are not be considered candidates for church membership or ordination in the Presbyterian Church in America.

Adopted by Savannah River Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 16, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE William Hatcher, stated clerk

OVERTURE 36 from Savannah River Presbytery (to CCB, OC) “Amend BCO 40-4 and 40-5 To Clarify the Meaning of ‘Credible Report”

Whereas, there has been various interpretations regarding the meaning of “credible report” in BCO 40-5; and

Whereas, these various interpretations have contended either that (1) a  
credible report may arise from any credible source presented to the court  
having appellate jurisdiction with respect to the court next below; or (2)  
a credible report may arise only upon referral of a matter from the  
General Assembly according to RAO 16-10.c; and

Whereas, BCO 40-4 allows that: “Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be distinctly recorded by them." and

Whereas, BCO 40-4 also states that: "If, therefore, the next higher court be  
well advised that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part  
of the lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the same,  
and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter as completely  
as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up by review of its records."  
and

Whereas, consequently when a court next below neglects to perform its duty  
under the Constitution; and further, fails to record its actions distinctly,  
the remedy is for the court with appellate jurisdiction to “be well advised  
that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred;" and

Whereas, since it is not clearly defined by what means the appellate court  
may "be well advised that any such neglect or irregularity has occurred;"  
and

<a id="ga47-p687"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=687 printed_page=685 -->

Whereas, when the lower court fails to distinctly record its actions as  
required, and further does not inform members who may be affected and  
harmed by these actions with notice in a timely manner, it results in  
members losing their right to file an Appeal (BCO 42) or a Complaint  
(BCO 43) in a timely manner; and

Whereas, courts can fail in the proper exercise of their responsibility to  
distinctly record their actions in such a manner that it is not discerned or  
discovered by the higher court during the process of the regular review  
of the lower court's records, the higher court during its review of records  
is not able to determine or judge the validity of the record; and

Whereas, BCO 40-4 and BCO 40-5 grant the higher court the right to review  
the record again once the higher court has received credible reports of  
"any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of  
such court;" and these credible reports can come from any credible  
source, which then requires the higher court to review "any important  
delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings of such court."

Therefore, to clarify the meaning of "credible reports" this overture recommends that BCO 40-4 and BCO 40-5 be amended with the following (additional wording underlined):

40-4. Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their  
duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices  
may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross  
character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in  
their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be  
distinctly recorded by them. In any of these cases their records  
will by no means exhibit to the higher court a full view of their  
proceedings. If, therefore, the next higher court be well  
advised, through a credible report as defined in BCO 40-5, that  
any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part of the  
lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the  
same, and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter  
as completely as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up  
by review of its records.

40-5. When any court having appellate jurisdiction shall  
receive a credible report, with respect to the court next below  
of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional  
proceedings of such court, the first step shall be to cite the court  
alleged to have offended to appear before the court having  
appellate jurisdiction, or its commission, by representative or

<a id="ga47-p688"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=688 printed_page=686 -->

in writing, at a specified time and place, and to show what the  
lower court has done or failed to do in the case in question. A  
credible report may arise either from a review of the records of  
the lower court as required under BCO 40-1; or from other  
credible means that make known to the court having appellate  
jurisdiction of the court next below of any important  
delinquency or grossly unconstitutional proceedings; and/or  
where the right of members to file a timely Appeal (BCO 42)  
or Complaint (BCO 43) was abridged by a lower court's failure  
to conduct proper proceedings or to provide timely notices.  
When a court acts on any credible report, the parties shall be  
the lower court and the court having appellate jurisdiction.

The court thus issuing the citation may reverse or redress the  
proceedings of the court below in other than judicial cases; or  
it may censure the delinquent court; or it may remit the whole  
matter to the delinquent court with an injunction to take it up  
and dispose of it in a constitutional manner; or it may stay all  
further proceedings in the case; as circumstances may require.

### As amended the provision would read:

40-4. Courts may sometimes entirely neglect to perform their  
duty, by which neglect heretical opinions or corrupt practices  
may be allowed to gain ground; or offenders of a very gross  
character may be suffered to escape; or some circumstances in  
their proceedings of very great irregularity may not be  
distinctly recorded by them. In any of these cases their records  
will by no means exhibit to the higher court a full view of their  
proceedings. If, therefore, the next higher court be well  
advised, through a credible report as defined in BCO 40-5, that  
any such neglect or irregularity has occurred on the part of the  
lower court, it is incumbent on it to take cognizance of the  
same, and to examine, deliberate and judge in the whole matter  
as completely as if it had been recorded, and thus brought up  
by review of its records.

40-5. When any court having appellate jurisdiction shall  
receive a credible report, with respect to the court next below  
of any important delinquency or grossly unconstitutional  
proceedings of such court, the first step shall be to cite the court

<a id="ga47-p689"></a>

alleged to have offended to appear before the court having  
appellate jurisdiction, or its commission, by representative or  
in writing, at a specified time and place, and to show what the  
lower court has done or failed to do in the case in question. A  
credible report may arise either from a review of the records of  
the lower court as required under BCO 40-1; or from other

### OVERTURE 37 from James River Presbytery “Assembly Statement on Same-sex Attraction”

Whereas, there is tremendous cultural pressure in the United States in these days concerning homosexuality and sexual sin; and

Whereas, there are many people inside and outside the church who struggle with same-sex attraction and gender confusion; and

Whereas, the Revoice organization held a conference in 2018 which discussed how to improve the way the church ministers to people who struggle with same-sex attraction, encouraging them to uphold the Biblical sexual ethic; and

Whereas, we acknowledge and affirm that Revoice showed love to people struggling with these sins; and

Whereas, we acknowledge and affirm that the Church has not always shown love to people who struggle with these sins; and

(to OC)

<a id="ga47-p690"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=690 printed_page=688 -->

Whereas, the Presbyterian Church in America, as part of its duty under the Great Commission, desires to better minister to people who struggle with same-sex attraction; Whereas, the Church commends the faithfulness of Christians struggling with same-sex attraction who are seeking to remain faithful to a Biblical sexual ethic; Therefore, the 47th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America affirms that:

1. That all persons are born sinners justly deserving God's wrath and condemnation and inherit both the guilt of our first parents as well as corruption. (Rom 5:12)

2. That outside of Christ, men and women are enslaved to corruption which enslaves the thinking of all persons and distorts God's created order. (Eph 2:1-8) That Christ has purchased not only the faith of his saints on the cross by which they are made just in God's sight but has also broken the power of sin/corruption to enslave His sheep. (Rom 8:1-11)

4. That Christ unites sinners to Himself, though they be corrupt through and through, but he does not leave them in corruption but subdues their corruption and produces holiness in them. (Rom 5:12-22, 6:1- 10; Col. 2:15)

5. That corruption draws all toward sinful desires whether they be anger, disobedience, pride, hatred, lusts, or unnatural attractions. (Eph 2:1-3).

6. That the Scriptures consistently exhort believers to reckon themselves dead to sin/corruption and alive to Christ (Rom 6:5-11, 1 Cor 6:9-11)

7. That “sexual orientation” is a modern invention describing men and women as being on a spectrum of sexual attraction or desire, and is not a Biblical category.

8. That the use of terms such as “Gay Christian,” “Same Sex Attracted Christian,” “Alcoholic Christian,” “Lustful Christian,” “Greedy Christian," or any other corrupt desire is not consistent with our union with Christ. Such descriptors of our fallenness must not be used as an identity marker but must rather be humbly submitted to Christ who provides our primary identity as Christians. (1 Cor. 6:9-11)

9. That the pull toward same-sex lust is not morally neutral but arises from our fallen nature, and with all other temptations must be mortified by the power which Christ supplies. (Rom. 1:18-27)

10. That Christians will struggle all their lives with sin and that the Church should never promise healing from sin in this life but the 688

<a id="ga47-p691"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=691 printed_page=689 -->

## APPENDIX V

Spirit's strength to kill unholy desires and to grow holy desires. (Rom 8:9-11)

11. That no temptation has overtaken any of us except that which is common to man and the Church must, therefore, be a place where we encourage one another in the battle against indwelling sin. (1 Cor 10:13)

12. That while there is a place for conferences and support groups, the Church is a haven for sinners and we should find solidarity in this common battle with sin not only with others who struggle exactly the same but primarily among those in our local congregation who share a common Savior. (Hebrews 10:25, Gal. 6:10)

Adopted by James River Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 13, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE Jeremy L. Pryor, stated clerk

OVERTURE 38 from Georgia Foothills Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Establish a Study Committee on Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault”(Version 7)

Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25- 27; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are "against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society;17 and Whereas, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their

17For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: "More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime" (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online at http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf). 689

<a id="ga47-p692"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=692 printed_page=690 -->

care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and Whereas, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; Therefore, be it resolved that the Georgia Foothills Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault;

- **(2)** the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins;

- **(3)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(4)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(5)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with the Georgia Foothills Presbytery committed to offer $1,000; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly.

Adopted by Georgia Foothills Presbytery at its stated meeting, April 9, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Don Aldin, stated clerk

the Resolution below requires no higher court voting or constitutional  
amendment; and  
Whereas, the PCA has an institution already in existence that could launch  
and nurture many gifts for ministry by our godly sisters, with no required  
BCO changes or time-consuming debates; and  
Whereas, most of our female members do not desire ordination as an  
aspiration or prerequisite to carry out gospel ministry; and  
Whereas, rather than dividing and quarreling over this matter in the years to  
come; and  
Whereas, BCO 9-7 presently allows Sessions to recruit godly women in  
ministries in the local church under the authority and norms of Scripture;  
and  
Whereas, Paul differentiates between the Deacons and The Women in 1  
Timothy 3:8-12; and  
Whereas, the PCA could devote itself more to mission, evangelism, unity,  
and edification by implementing the Resolution below, rather than  
dividing over this issue in the courts of the church;  
Therefore, be it resolved that those churches wishing to acknowledge and  
support Women leaders be authorized to select and appoint the officers  
of their Women in the Church [previously known as WIC, or more  
recently “Women's Ministry"] with the laying on of hands to serve in  
the local church and assist the deacons in caring for those in need and  
distress. The manner of appointment or election of these officers shall be  
the discretion of each Session.

## APPENDIX V

OVERTURE 41 from Heritage Presbytery (to MTW) “Direct CMTW to Amend its Guidelines to Implement CMTW’s 'Statement on Valuing Women in MTW,' so that only Ordained Elders Will Be Allowed to Serve in the Roles of Team Leader, Regional Director, and International Director within MTW."

Whereas on January 9, 2019, the Committee on Mission To the World (CMTW) adopted a “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW"; and Whereas MTW subsequently proposed guidelines to implement the “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW" that were distributed to missionaries on January 11, 2019; and Whereas the MTW guidelines affirm "that women may serve in leadership roles within MTW, recognizing that only ordained elders exercise ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches" [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 3, paragraph 3.]; and Whereas the MTW guidelines also affirm "there has been no MTW policy regarding women serving in these leadership roles..." [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 4, paragraph 1.]; and Whereas the MTW guidelines initiate a new policy that allows women to serve in authority over men within MTW in the roles of team leader, regional director, and international director [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, page 8, #3.]; and Whereas Heritage Presbytery and other presbyteries of the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) are charged to provide spiritual oversight for ordained elders who come from within our bounds, but who serve under MTW [See BCO 8-3 &13-2.]; Therefore be it resolved that Heritage Presbytery hereby overture the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to direct CMTW to ensure that MTW amend its guidelines to implement CMTW's “Statement on Valuing Women in MTW," so that only ordained elders will be allowed to serve in the roles of team leader, regional director, and international director within MTW.

Rationale: While CMTW’s intention of “supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW's global ministry..." [see the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 698] is commendable, the MTW guidelines actually hinder some of our women from serving in MTW by creating an untenable crisis of conscience for them. Therefore, the MTW guidelines discourage some of the very sisters in Christ that CMTW's "Statement on Valuing Women in MTW" intends to support in their missionary service.

693

<a id="ga47-p696"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=696 printed_page=694 -->

Secondly, the MTW guidelines allow a woman to hold a position of authority within MTW in which she cannot exercise ecclesiastical authority over a man. And the MTW guidelines concede this would require an ordained man to fulfill some of her position's responsibilities. [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 700, #3.] But an obvious consequence of such an awkward arrangement would be questions about what a woman in such a position is and is not allowed to do. For example, MTW's Policy Manual currently indicates the team leader position has very broad authority, including “spiritual care" over those on the missionary team. Yet the MTW guidelines leave the team leader position potentially open to non-elders. Therefore, the MTW guidelines are unwise because they can lead to placing women in difficult positions, while causing unnecessary confusion and conflict within a missionary team. Lastly, the MTW guidelines cite the Report of the Ad Interim Committee on Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church to the 45th General Assembly of the PCA, as a primary reason MTW is allowing women to have authority over men within MTW – even potentially over ordained elders. [See the attached Statement with Guidelines, p. 698.] But the 46th General Assembly rejected two overtures that would have allowed women to serve on PCA agency boards. [See Overtures 13 and 26.]

Adopted by Heritage Presbytery at its stated meeting, May 14, 2019 Attested by /s/ RE Conrad W Judy Jr., Stated Clerk
