Statement on Valuing Women in MTW Adopted by the Committee on Mission to the World January 9, 2019

Statement Adopted by Committee on Mission to the World:

MTW values all women as created in the image of God. Under Scripture's authority and in our doctrinal view of ordination, we affirm that female disciples of Christ are co-heirs of the kingdom, co-laborers in the work of the gospel, gifted by the Spirit as members of the body of Christ and called to use these gifts for the building up of the Church and for the extension of the Kingdom of God throughout the world. Furthermore, the MTW community deeply needs the gifts and glory of God uniquely expressed in women. Therefore, MTW is committed to supporting 694

<a id="ga47-p697"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=697 printed_page=695 -->

## APPENDIX V

and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW's global ministry as together we show and tell the gospel of God's grace. In keeping with this statement, we affirm that women may serve in leadership roles within MTW, recognizing that only ordained elders exercise ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches. Reasons for Creation of the Statement: First, the growing desire from our denomination to encourage women to use their gifts for the service of the church are reflected in the recommendation passed at the 45th General Assembly of the PCA, stating "that sessions, presbyteries, and the General Assembly strive to develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge and wisdom of godly women in the local, regional, and national church..." The spirit of this recommendation is to actively look for ways in which women can utilize their gifts in the local and larger church context. Second, women have been serving in various leadership capacities in MTW on different fields, in the home office, and in specific roles. In each of these contexts, those who made these appointments ensured that their leadership is in accord with our complementarian view of men and women's roles in the church. The problem that emerged, however, was when women leaders were invited to global leadership meetings, questions arose from other MTW leaders and missionaries as to whether women should attend those meetings, and about the legitimacy of female leadership roles in light of passages such as 1 Timothy 2:12. What has complicated the matter is the fact that there has been no MTW policy regarding women serving in these leadership roles, nor has there been an organization-wide discussion on these issues. What has resulted is that faithful women serving in leadership are put in difficult positions, having to defend their leadership positions and presence at leadership meetings. It is in this context that we have initiated a discussion on women serving in leadership in MTW, and on deploying the God-given gifting of our MTW women, for the service of the Church. Field leadership has participated in this discussion in various ways, including writing of papers expressing a variety of opinion submitted to Committee on Mission to the World (CMTW). These discussions and papers were used by CMTW in their deliberations as they sought how to best articulate a policy for MTW on women serving in MTW.

695

<a id="ga47-p698"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=698 printed_page=696 -->

Purpose of the Statement: “So God created man in His own image, in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them. And God blessed them." Genesis 1:27- 28a “In accordance with Scripture and the Reformed Confession, (is) the idea that a human being does not bear or have the image of God, but that he or she is the image of God" – Herman Bavinck, Reformed Dogmatics: God and Creation

CMTW's statement calls our missional community to value all women, and to recognize and deploy women's gifting in building the Church and extending the Kingdom of Jesus Christ around the world. In addition, our General Assembly through the Ad Interim Committee report has encouraged us to consider applicable recommendations from their report on “Women Serving in the Ministry of the Church," amended and adopted by the 45th General Assembly of the PCA.

One aspect of the CMTW statement focuses on women in leadership roles in MTW. This leadership affirmation is part of CMTW's encouragement to our missionary community to be “supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW's global ministry." As part of any discussion on leadership, we also affirm that all MTW leadership roles are based on a biblical model of servant leadership that does not seek to wield power over others, whether leadership is exercised by a man or a woman. MTW further recognizes that application of this portion of the statement regarding women serving in leadership roles in MTW may lead to specific and local questions of implementation, because of our shared desire to ensure that ecclesiastical authority over churches or church plants is reserved for men. Therefore, the Senior Leadership of MTW has endeavored to provide a list of considerations as a framework for thinking through application of this portion of the statement. Recommendations from the 45th PCA General Assembly18: These three recommendations from the adopted Recommendations from the Ad Interim Committee report are those that have particular applicability to our work in Mission to the World.

18 From the Report of the Ad Interim Committee on Women serving in the Ministry of the Church, to the 45th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America, as amended and adopted. 696

<a id="ga47-p699"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=699 printed_page=697 -->

## APPENDIX V

1. That sessions, presbyteries, and the General Assembly recognize that, from the founding of the PCA, there has been a variety of views and practices regarding the ways in which women may serve the Lord and the church within scriptural and constitutional parameters, without ordination, and that such mutual respect for said views and practices continues. Rationale: The Scriptures and the constitution of the PCA state that offices of the church are only open to qualified and ordained men. But the committee also recognizes that the Scriptures and the constitution of the PCA give freedom to its churches with regard to varying views and practices by its churches in the ways in which women may serve the Lord and the church. This freedom of view and practice has also been part of the PCA's history... Therefore, the committee recommends that ruling and teaching elders continue this recognition of freedom within PCA churches to utilize women's gifts within the scriptural and constitutional parameters, without ordination.... this freedom of views and practices within PCA churches where Scripture and the constitution allow for freedom is a strength of the denomination and should be valued by the whole church.

2. That sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly strive to develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom of godly women in the local, regional, and national church, and particularly consider overtures that would allow qualified women to serve on appropriate committees and agencies within the church. Rationale: The Scriptures teach that the Holy Spirit has given gifts to the church for the glory of God and the edification of the church (Rom. 12:3- 8; 1 Cor. 12:1-11; Eph. 4:11- 16). Churches should strive to identify, develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom of all our members.... The committee further encourages PCA churches to utilize the gifts, skills, and knowledge of women by particularly and especially promoting and recruiting qualified women to serve.

3. That sessions, presbyteries and the General Assembly consider how they can affirm and include underprivileged and underrepresented women in the PCA.

Rationale: After Jesus rose from the dead, He commanded His apostles: “Therefore, go make disciples of all nations” (Matt. 28:18). Jesus, our 697

<a id="ga47-p700"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=700 printed_page=698 -->

great King, prescribes the mission of His church, which, in part, is to ensure the nations become His disciples (cf. WCF 7.6). The overflow of the Great Commission is revealed in Acts. The names in Acts 13:1 demonstrate that Jesus' disciples took His commission seriously. Indeed, people from different ethnic backgrounds were coming to faith in Christ. Unfortunately, the PCA, though it upholds the mandate to make disciples of the nations, has yet to see the demographics in diverse communities reflected in Mission to the World. Therefore, as the MTW considers the Great Commission afresh, we should affirm that intentionally reaching the nations in their communities is not an addition to the church's ministry. It is a demand, even command, by Jesus as a principal part of their church's ministry. Acts 6:1-7 sets precedent for affirming the underprivileged. Whether male or female, everyone deserved equal treatment in Christ's church (cf. Jas. 2:1-13).

Application of Recommendations: Each of these recommendations made by the Report and adopted by the 45th General Assembly applies to Mission to the World, in that each of recommendation is made to PCA presbyteries and to General Assembly. Mission to the World, as a committee of the General Assembly, is thereby encouraged to adopt these recommendations. We believe these recommendations are commended by CMTW to every member of MTW, as summed up in the Statement: "Therefore, MTW is committed to supporting and equipping our sisters in Christ as they exercise their gifts and abilities throughout MTW's global ministry as together we show and tell the gospel of God's grace." Specifically, these recommendations encourage Mission to the World to:

1. Recognize various views and practices in the PCA within “scriptural and constitutional parameters," and to respect and support those various views and practices;

2. Strive to develop, recognize, and utilize the gifts, skills, knowledge, and wisdom of godly women, and promoting and recruiting them to serve.

3. Consider how to affirm and include underprivileged and underrepresented women in Mission to the World. The CMTW-adopted Statement on Valuing Women seeks to encourage everyone in Mission to the World to consider and embrace these recommendations from the General Assembly. There are various ways field teams and leadership may go about following these recommendations. 698

<a id="ga47-p701"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=701 printed_page=699 -->

## APPENDIX V

For example: spending a season in prayer about how to implement these recommendations; inviting women to attend leadership development events in order to identify and increase their skills and gifts; including the voices of women in brainstorming, vision casting, or other future-oriented planning sessions; conducting a “gifts survey” of a field team, including all members of the team; asking with intentionality if there might be a woman who could serve in open or new leadership positions. Any of these and more would be helpful starting points that lead to intentionally looking for opportunities to deploy gifts not currently being used. Considerations for MTW Field Operations: The concluding paragraph in the CMTW-adopted Statement on Valuing Women may be a challenging portion for regions and teams to implement, and may lead to questions of application. That portion of the statement reads: "In keeping with this statement, we affirm that women may serve in leadership roles within MTW, recognizing that only ordained elders exercise ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches." In order to assist teams and regions in making decisions, this list of considerations is provided as a guide to assist in thinking through specific application. First, however, is what is meant by "ecclesiastical authority over church plants or churches?" Helpful here are two paragraphs from the PCA Book of Church Order, chapter 3:

3-2. Ecclesiastical power, which is wholly spiritual, is twofold. The officers exercise it sometimes severally, as in preaching the Gospel, administering the Sacraments, reproving the erring, visiting the sick, and comforting the afflicted, which is the power of order; and they exercise it sometimes jointly in Church courts, after the form of judgment, which is the power of jurisdiction.

3-6. The exercise of ecclesiastical power, whether joint or several,  
has the divine sanction when in conformity with the statutes  
enacted by Christ, the Lawgiver, and when put forth by courts or  
by officers appointed thereunto in His Word.  
Ecclesiastical power, as defined by the BCO, means that power that is  
exercised by a church officer when serving in the role of his office, or by a  
Church court, such as a Session, Presbytery, or General Assembly.  
Therefore, this portion of the statement indicates a woman can serve in  
leadership, other than in roles that would exercise (ecclesiastical) authority  
over church plants or churches.

699

<a id="ga47-p702"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=702 printed_page=700 -->

With this understanding, here is a list of considerations that could help in thinking through MTW leadership appointments and clarifying when the person in those positions would exercise ecclesiastical authority over church or church plants:

1. If a leader has no direct authority over ordained elders serving in a church or church planting context, appointment of a woman as leader should be considered.

2. Would a leader have direct authority over an elder in the elder's exercise of his ecclesiastical responsibilities? If so, then an ordained elder is necessary.

3. Would a leader have direct leadership authority for one or more ordained elders serving in a church or in a church planting context? If so, then:

- **a.** Would that leader have leadership responsibilities apart from those responsibilities which are ordinarily the responsibility of ordained elders or church courts? AND

- **b.** Is there another ordained elder in the region in line authority to whom church matters (apart from applicable church court) can be deferred, in consultation with the leader? If so, appointment of a woman or other non-ordained leader is possible in that leadership role.

4. Does a specific national context or partnership only welcome ordained elders as partners in leadership roles? We commend discussion with national partners and local leaders when considering these appointments so that the local context is well understood. We propose there are situations in which the degree of the exclusion of women or non-ordained men from participation in a culture must be challenged in healthy ways. At the same time, there may be situations in which teaching and biblical education of partners might need to precede appointment of nonordained leaders in contexts that are culturally (but not biblically) exclusive, so as not to offend national partners in such contexts. However a biblical “critical contextualization19” should encourage us, and our partners, in a direction that embraces men and women serving in appropriate roles in the church when the leadership roles are not exercising ecclesiastical authority over churches or church plants. Conclusion Our desire is to see our missionary community value our women colleagues

19Dr. Paul Heibert, Critical Contextualization. International Bulletin 11:3:104-112. July. Reprinted in The Best in Theology: Volume Two, J. 1. Packer, General Editor. Wheaton: Christianity Today. pp. 387-400.

700

<a id="ga47-p703"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=703 printed_page=701 -->

## APPENDIX V

throughout our organization, seeking to deploy the gifts that God has given His Church through every one of our members. At the same time, we seek to affirm and uphold the ecclesiastical authority of the Church through qualified ordained men. MTW, the Committee on Mission to the World, and the 44th General Assembly of the PCA recognize we can, and must, seek to further encourage and challenge ourselves to pursue these recommendations, that the Church may be strengthened with all of the gifts of the Giver, for His glory.

OVERTURE 42 from Chicago Metro Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Establish Study Committee on Sexuality”

Whereas, in recent years a dramatic shift in cultural norms and attitudes away from Biblical teaching and morality concerning human sexuality has taken place; and Whereas, the current cultural climate presents an apologetic and evangelistic challenge to the Church as she seeks to articulate the Biblical teaching on human sexuality clearly and effectively to those outside; and Whereas, this cultural climate also fosters increasingly complex pastoral situations as the Church seeks to minister to those who struggle with issues related to their own sexuality; and Whereas, some of the flock in our midst are among those hard-pressed with temptation that manifests itself through same sex-attraction or a confused sexual identity, and many sessions may feel overwhelmed or underequipped to minister to them; and Whereas, though the PCA issued statements in 1977, 1996, and 1999 on the Biblical view concerning homosexuality, these statements were delivered before the more recent cultural changes with their attendant challenges, and the PCA has yet to undertake an extensive study of the topic; and Whereas, the PCA has the Biblical, theological, and confessional resources to apply the unchanging gospel to the issues surrounding human sexuality in our current cultural environment; Therefore, be it resolved that the 47th General Assembly create an Ad- Interim Committee (AIC) to study the topic of human sexuality with particular attention to the issues of homosexuality, same- sex attraction, and transgenderism, and prepare a report which:

OVERTURE 43 from Metro Atlanta Presbytery (to AC, OC) “Formation of a Study Committee on Domestic Abuse and Sexual Assault”(Version 8) Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse, including physical, emotional, and verbal abuse, and sexual assault are expressly forbidden in scripture (Deuteronomy 22:25-27; Eph. 5:25-29; 2 Timothy 3:2-5; 1 Peter 3:7; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are “against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society as well as the Church; and Whereas, these sins cause a complex set of physical, emotional, spiritual, and psychological responses—including immense shame, fear and anxiety, depression, trauma, isolation, anger, and denial—that persist with varying levels of severity throughout life; and since these heinous sins do lasting damage to every aspect of a victims life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for the vulnerable and those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance in each case in accordance with applicable law (Ezekiel 34:1-24; James 1:27; BCO 8-3; 27-4); and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations (cf. the Roman Catholic Church and the Southern Baptist Convention) but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly of the PCA; and

703

<a id="ga47-p706"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=706 printed_page=704 -->

Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, the PCA report on “Divorce and Remarriage” was limited in its focus and does not adequately define the scope and nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault nor adequately address many pastoral concerns regarding the care of those victimized by such sins; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and Whereas, the Rules of Discipline protect against unjust accusation (BCO 31- 8), they also make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; Therefore, be it resolved that Metro Atlanta Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for justly and lawfully protecting against these sins, for providing safety for potential victims who come forward, and for responding to those guilty of these sins; and

- **(2)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(3)** the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins as well as ministry and counsel for those guilty of such sins;

- **(4)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and

- **(5)** to include in their report a definition of the scope and nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with Metro Atlanta Presbytery committed to offer $1,000; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for consideration by the 48th General Assembly. and the use of such terms as "sexual orientation," "gay," "sexual minorities," "gay Christian” and the “identity questions” it raises, etc., and whether such use constitutes profound doctrinal or perhaps practical error, and ought to be soundly condemned and censured or, on the other hand, tolerated, with proper caveats and qualifications; and Whereas doctrinal boundaries and pastoral applications of sensitive and/or controversial issues are best made by deliberative and collaborative debate, study, conversation, and consensus-building rather than by judicial fiat in investigations and trials, a principle that was demonstrated to be so helpful in the case of the Ad-Interim Committee on Divorce and Remarriage (1992) and the Ad-interim Committee on the Days of Creation (2000); and Whereas the peace and purity of the church as well as the integrity of and energy for the mission of the church to our secular culture is at stake in these current debates; and Whereas our Presbytery ad hoc committee appointed to investigate Memorial PCA's hosting of the 2018 Revoice conference, after giving careful consideration to the underlying theological, pastoral, and missiological matters, recommended that we overture the General Assembly for a further in-depth study/consensus-building committee for the purpose of coming to greater doctrinal clarity in pursuit of a deeper church unity on issues touching homosexuality;

Therefore, be it resolved that the 47th General Assembly create an Ad Interim Committee (AIC) to study the topic of sexuality with particular attention to the issue of where the church has failed in its ministry to same-sex-attracted men and women, and what the church ought to be doing now in its ministry to them, while neither compromising the gospel nor dulling the vitality of its message to lost people. The committee is tasked with preparing a report which: Shall seek, as much as consciences permit, to build a consensus on these difficult matters so as to secure a place, within trusted boundaries, for our wider church to grow in their witness to Christ and live at peace with one another; and Shall address: (1) the nature of temptation, sin, and repentance as regards same-sex-attraction; (2) the propriety of using terms like "gay," "gay Christian” when referring to a believer living with samesex attraction; (3) The status of "orientation" as a valid anthropological category; (4) the practice of “celibate partnerships" and “romantic coupling" for same-sex-attracted Christians; and O Shall include suggested ways to articulate and defend a Biblical understanding of homosexuality in the context of a culture that denies that understanding; and O Shall include an annotated bibliography of resources on sexuality which the Committee recommends for helping pastors and Sessions shepherd their people who live with same-sex attraction; and O This Committee may:

- **a.** report to the 48th GA in Birmingham (2020) any statement it adopts as a Committee, without needing to move it for GA adoption.

- **b.** recommend to the 48th GA any statement it believes would be prudent and warranted for the Assembly to adopt. Be it further resolved that the Moderator of the 47th General Assembly appoint the seven voting members who shall be either PCA teaching or PCA ruling elders (at least two of each kind), including members whose writings have included theological engagement on the issue and members who have had pastoral interaction with those struggling with same-sex attraction; and Be it further resolved that the Committee be permitted to recruit others, within the confines of its budget, to serve as its advisors, regardless of denomination or gender, with particular concern to secure those with experience in counseling those dealing with same-sex attraction; and

Whereas, the Word of God indicates that all human beings are created in the image of God (Genesis 1:26, 27) and therefore have great worth in God's sight, and Whereas, God's Word also indicates that human life is therefore of such value that to destroy that life for any reason other than that which God has prescribed, which is murder, is of such seriousness as to merit capital punishment (Genesis 9:5, 6), and

(WCF 31:4) to address matters which pertain to the civil magistrate, and Whereas, both the legalization of the murder of a helpless class, resulting in the loss of more than 51 million lives, and the forced subsidization of such by individuals opposed to it, constitute such an extraordinary case, Therefore, be it resolved that the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America officially, and on the basis of the inspired and authoritative Word of God, declare the following: We reaffirm our denomination's commitment on this pertinent, prevalent issue regarding the sanctity of life and our stance against abortion in particular. OVERTURE 47 from Missouri Presbytery (to AC, OC) "Formation of a Study Committee on Domestic Abuse and Sexual Assault”(Version 9)

Whereas, the sins of domestic abuse and sexual assault are expressly forbidden (2 Timothy 3:2-5; Jude 7; Exodus 21:15; Deuteronomy 22:25- 27; also WLC 135 and 139); and Whereas, these sins are especially heinous because they are "against the express letter of the law," "break many commandments," "admit of no reparation," and often involve various other aggravations (WLC 151); and Whereas, these sins are grievously prevalent in our society;21 and Whereas, these sins often produce in the victims a complex response of denial along with immense fear and shame that persist with varying severity throughout life (e.g., 2 Samuel 13:1-22); and Whereas, it is the responsibility of the elders of the church to exercise their authority, severally and jointly, to shepherd those who are under their care by guarding against such sinful behavior as much as possible, by wisely caring for those victimized by the sins of others, and by appropriately disciplining those guilty of such sins toward a full repentance; and Whereas, these sins have been a concerning subject of attention not only in other denominations but even in the proceedings of the 46th General Assembly; and Whereas, the 42nd General Assembly previously exhorted the PCA and its courts to respond boldly against one form of these sins, namely the sexual abuse of children; and Whereas, no standardized resources for pastoral care on these sins and their complex consequences exist for officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA; and Whereas, no clear guidelines for policy or practice with regard to these sins exist for the officers, church courts, and agencies in the PCA that would protect individuals and congregations; and

21 For example, the National Domestic Violence Hotline reports: "More than 1 in 3 women (35.6%) and more than 1 in 4 men (28.5%) in the United States have experienced rape, physical violence and/or stalking by an intimate partner in their lifetime" (available at http://www.thehotline.org/resources/statistics/, accessed 6/15/18). For further sobering statistics on sexual violence see the National Center for Injury Prevention and Controls report entitled Sexual Violence Surveillance: Uniform Definitions and Recommended Data Elements (Atlanta: Center for Disease Control, 2014; available online at http://www.cdc.gov/violenceprevention/pdf/sv_surveillance_definitionsl-2009-a.pdf). 711

<a id="ga47-p714"></a>

Whereas, the Rules of Discipline make no consideration for the unique heinousness of these sins and their practical effect on victims; Therefore, be it resolved that Missouri Presbytery hereby overtures the 47th General Assembly of the PCA to form a committee to study:

- **(1)** the nature of domestic abuse and sexual assault;

- **(2)** the pastoral resources available for the care of survivors of these sins;

- **(3)** the best practices and policy guidelines for elders, church courts, and agencies for protecting against these sins and for responding to them;

- **(4)** the possibility of changes to the Rules of Discipline that would appropriately protect victims of these sins within a biblical process; and

- **(5)** the possible need for repentance as a church; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall be appointed by the moderator, and shall include among its members or advisory members at least two subject-matter experts and at least two women; and Be it further resolved that the budget for the study committee be set at $15,000/year and that funds be derived from gifts to the AC designated for that purpose, with Missouri Presbytery committed to offer some money; and Be it further resolved that the committee shall present their findings and recommendations for adoption by the 48th General Assembly.

Adopted by Missouri Presbytery at its stated meeting on April 16, 2019 Attested by /s/ TE Timothy R. Butler, stated clerk

Ninth, that the churches of the Presbyterian Church in America are urged to redouble their efforts in biblical instruction on sex, sexuality, marriage, and family, and on God's will concerning the interrelation of and participation in all of these.

Grounds:

1. The previous overtures and statements approved by the General Assembly, while salutary, do not speak explicitly and strongly enough to the biblical specifics surrounding the issue.

716

<a id="ga47-p719"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=719 printed_page=717 -->

## APPENDIX V

2. These previous overtures contain nothing affirming and declaring the responsibility of the Church to discipline those who are sinning in this area.

3. These previous overtures include little regarding the responsibility of Christian political leaders to oppose abortion, or regarding their sin in being complicit in approving or promoting it through various legislation, and their consequent liability to church discipline. Inasmuch as there are many professing Christians in the political arena who regard their political activity and commitments as unaccountable to church discipline and who thus feel confident in participating in the promotion of abortion on demand and its funding with no spiritual consequences, this needs to be addressed explicitly and officially by the Church, and such attention is long overdue.

4. The scientific, historical, and moral mythology surrounding abortion and its justification, including the deceptive and false context of the Roe V. Wade decision, and the nature and history of Planned Parenthood, needs to be officially and comprehensively addressed in the rationale for the Church's position. This has not been adequately accomplished in previous overtures, and is the reason for the extensive “Whereas” section of the proposed overture.

5. The secular humanistic culture concomitant with abortion on demand is becoming more brazen and aggressive daily. This requires a forceful, frank, and aggressive response from the Church. Abortion is an atrocity. Language which mollifies portrayal of the extreme evil of its nature, or which fails to speak accurately and honestly about the ramifications of its practice, is a dereliction of the duty of ministers of the Word and shepherds who are called to tell the sheep the truth, whatever consequences that might entail. To water down the truth in an effort to be “temperate” is in this context to unfaithful to our calling.

6. Sound and truly loving pastoral practice brings those who have sinned to an awareness of the heinousness of their sin, leading to godly sorrow which produces true repentance unto life. A too hasty application of comfort to those who have sinned in this way makes such a process impossible. Discretion and prudence are needed in the application of truth to individual cases, discerning where a person is in the process of repentance, but refraining from strong public statements and warnings regarding the practice of abortion does not well serve those who are grieving over their sin. Rather, true repentance joined with genuine faith in the justifying grace of Christ should render such individuals the strongest proponents of such language.

Overture 23 from Tennessee Valley Presbytery, "Oppose Research on Transplantation of Fetal Tissue" Whereas National Institutes of Health (NIH), a federal agency under the Department of Health and Human Services is responsible for supporting the majority of health sciences research, and Whereas NIH is in the process of deciding whether to lift the moratorium on the funding of fetal tissue research, and Whereas NIH has accepted the unanimous recommendation from the Advisory Council to the Director, which states, according to the January 1989 issue of the FASEB Newsletter (the official newsletter of the Federation of American Societies of Experimental Biology), "The federal government should resume funding research on the therapeutic transplantation of fetal tissues from elective abortions as treatment for diabetes and Parkinson's disease," and Whereas we, as members of the evangelical, Bible-believing denomination, The Presbyterian Church in America, believe that elective abortions are against the teaching of the Bible, and Whereas we believe that the arguments to use fetal tissue obtained from elective abortions would be a seductive, though perhaps unintended, way to convince the general public that elective abortions are in the public interest if the tissues so obtained may be used for transplantations to relieve human suffering, Now therefore be it resolved that the Tennessee Valley Presbytery respectfully overture the 17th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) to express its moral conviction to the 721

The 27th General Assembly of the PCA reaffirms with united voice the sanctity of human life under the protection of the Sixth Commandment. And to that end,

1. The Stated Clerk is requested to do the following:

- **a.** Remind all the churches and presbyteries of the continuing availability of its published report on the sanctity of Human Life adopted by the Sixth General Assembly.

- **b.** That his letter to the churches regarding the actions of the 27th General Assembly repeat recommendations 2, 3, 5, 6, and 8 urging our churches and presbyteries to seek God's enablement and grace to implement them in light of the continued tragedy of abortion on demand in America.

Grounds:

- **a)** The Holy Spirit, speaking infallibly in Scripture, declares that human life is sacred, and that it begins at conception.

- **b)** This authoritative declaration by Almighty God makes the protection of all human life from the moment of conception to the moment of birth an inescapable moral duty for all men.

- **c)** The taking of the life of an unborn person is a violation of the sixth commandment, “Thou shall not murder," and is in fact premeditated murder.

- **d)** A considerable number of our elected and appointed government leaders want to make and keep legal the killing of the unborn for any and every reason.

- **e)** This assault on the unborn calls for a unified effort by Christians of all denominations to protect the unborn child from the moment of conception to the moment of birth and afterwards.

- **f)** Each and every person will one day stand before our sovereign God to give an account for his or her life, and whether or not that life was lived under the Lordship of Jesus Christ, the Lord of life.

Whereas the Holy Spirit, speaking infallibly in Scripture, declares that human life is sacred, and that it begins at conception; and Whereas this authoritative declaration by Almighty God makes the protection of all human life from the moment of conception to the moment of birth an inescapable moral duty for all men; and Whereas the taking of the life of an unborn person is a violation of the sixth commandment, "Thou shall not murder," and is in fact premeditated murder; and Whereas a considerable number of our elected and appointed government leaders want to make and keep legal the killing of the unborn for any and every reason; and Whereas this assault on the unborn calls for a unified effort by Christians of all dominations to protect the unborn child from the moment of conception to the moment of birth and afterwards; and Whereas each and every person will one day stand before our sovereign God to give an account for his or her life, and whether or not that life was lived under the Lordship of Jesus Christ, the Lord of life; Therefore be it resolved by the Presbyterian Church in America, that we will encourage all our members to immediately begin to approach professing Christians in all denominations:

To join with the entire Body of Christ for the protection of the unborn, acting in solidarity with other denominations in prayer and obedience to God, by whose sovereign might alone the scourge of legalized abortion will be broken; To speak prophetically against the culture of death, confronting it in the power of God's truth; To hold our culture accountable before the binding and unchallengeable authority of God's Holy Word over every man, woman, institution, and nation, in every area of life; To lovingly call offending parties to repentance in Jesus Christ, and restoration by the Holy Spirit to new obedience; To proclaim the authoritative truth of God, both to our own members and in the public square, concerning God's righteous demands upon the judicial, legislative, and executive branches of our government at every level.

Overture 43 from Savannah River Presbytery (to OC) "Expression of Support for Sanctity of Life and Marriage"

Whereas the Bible states that when there is a conflict between God's Law and human law, we must obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29), and Whereas the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution specifically prohibits Congress from establishing any law "prohibiting the free exercise of religion," and Whereas the environment for religious freedom worsens day by day in the United States, and Whereas some Christians today – including employers, chaplains, and others, must choose between being faithful to their Biblical convictions regarding the sanctity of human life and the sanctity of marriage, or face punitive federal government penalties, and Whereas God calls His Church to bear prophetic witness to His Truth in human society, and Whereas the Presbyterian Church in America, of which the Savannah River Presbytery is a member, is on record regarding the sanctity of human life and of marriage in accordance with that Truth; therefore Be it resolved that Savannah River Presbytery hereby go on record expressing its gratitude to and prayers for corporations, public and private for-profit and non-profit entities, chaplains and others who have taken a stand for the sanctity of human life, and to the Christian men and women in private businesses facing fines, penalties, and ostracism for declining out of religious conviction to provide their services for samesex marriage ceremonies, and Be it further resolved that Savannah River Presbytery call upon the 42nd General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America to adopt this resolution.

Adopted by Savannah River Presbytery at its Stated Meeting, April 15, 2014 Attested by/s/ RE William L Hatcher, stated clerk

tenets of our Christian faith. God has abundantly blessed you in so many  
ways including the significant growth of the PCA since your founding in

1973. The influence of your churches, schools, leaders and many ministries extends far beyond the PCA to bless us all and we are grateful. Your membership in the National Association of Evangelicals has long contributed to the significant and ongoing influence you have on our forty denominations and many evangelical organizations and ministries. PCA leaders are multiple and exemplary on the NAE board and staff. You evidence a fulfillment of the description on the PCA website that "We long to join in cooperative ministry with other parts of the universal church to pursue God's global mission." Your engagement with other evangelicals is well described on the first page when searching PCA on the internet: “The PCA is Reformed in theology, Presbyterian in government, and active in missions. ### COMMUNICATION 2

From The Reformed Church of Quebec Église réformée du Québec Interchurch Committee May 14, 2019 Fraternal Greetings to the 47th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America

Dear fathers and brothers in Christ,

Our Saviour calls us to be the lights of the world. We are thankful to be that light amongst the eight million people living in the province of Quebec, Canada. The Église réformée du Québec (ERQ) is the only French-speaking Reformed confessional witness in the province of Quebec. The ERQ is composed of a total of 360 souls worshiping in five local congregations. Our witness is small, like a nightlight, but by God's grace shining brightly. Our light has been shining in many ways, particularly through Reformed literature. In the French-speaking world, there is a growing interest in Reformed theology and practice. Best sellers include books written by pastors Kevin DeYoung, Tim Keller, John Piper, and R.C. Sproul. We are feeding that hunger for solid, Reformed teaching. For instance, Pastor Paulin Bédard writes, translates and prepares Reformed instructional material for publication on the website, Ressources chrétiennes. More than 3,700 articles are available free of charge to pastors and Christians throughout the French-speaking world, particularly in developing countries in French-speaking Africa. Our congregation in Quebec City is publishing several books under the banner Éditions La Rochelle, the name of the first French confession penned by John Calvin. Publications include French translations of John Sartelle's booklet, What Christian Parents Should Know about Infant Baptism; Calvin Cumming's The Covenant of Grace; Louis Berkhof's A Summary of Christian Doctrine; Mark Jones' Knowing Christ; and O. Palmer Robertson's The Christ of the Covenant. In celebration of the 400th anniversary of the synod of Dort, we published John Benton's Evangelistic Calvinism and Paulin Bédard's Le solide fondement du salut, an in-depth study of the Canons of Dort. Please pray for the Reformed witness in the province of Quebec, Canada as the Lord raises up workers for the harvest. Our synod recently granted licensure to two brothers, Blaise Tsabang and George-Émile Durand, even

730

<a id="ga47-p733"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=47 pdf_page=733 printed_page=731 -->

## APPENDIX W

as they complete their studies at Farel Reformed Theological Seminary. The seminary is directed by PCA missionary, John Garnet Zoellner, who has faithfully served the Reformed Church in Quebec for more than thirty years. Finally, even as you partner with us in the Quebec mission, we are seeking to be missional. Our Montreal congregation is sponsoring a Syrian refugee family. Our Quebec City congregation is sending a missionary worker to Lyon, France to work as an administrator of a Christian radio network. Our members, who are a minority of minorities – less than one percent of the Quebec population profess an evangelical faith – seek to be light in the world through their good works and their word of testimony. In a world increasingly secular, individualistic, materialistic, hedonistic – in short, a world increasingly dark, our nightlight shines more distinctly. We pray for the Lord's blessing upon your assembly, its deliberations and its decisions. May the Lord continue to advance the reign of the Lord Jesus Christ through your faithful witness. With brotherly affection, Ben Westerveld Pastor For the Interchurch Committee of the ERQ
